jobs.title: Operations Campus Manager
jobs.description:
We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.
 
Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.
 
Location & Team Gatherings
We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of the listed location above.
 
We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; and Toronto, ON.


About this role
 
As Campus Operations Manager — Meitner Energy Center on Intersect's Operations team, you'll hold the premier asset leadership role on-site in Pampa, Texas, serving as the single point of accountability for the safety, performance, and long-term reliability of our flagship multi-technology generation campus powering co-located Google data center infrastructure. You'll orchestrate a behind-the-meter energy ecosystem combining approximately 500 MW of solar PV, 650 MW of wind generation, 1 GW / 2 GWh of battery energy storage, 300 MW of fast-start reciprocating gas generation, and a 345kV/34.5kV breaker-and-a-half switching station—including a 300 MW BESS and 300 MW gas microgrid configured for islanded operation to sustain critical data center load independent of the ERCOT grid.
 
You'll direct an integrated leadership tier of Solar, Wind, BESS, Gas, and High Voltage / Substation Site Managers alongside internalized maintenance teams to maximize campus Equivalent Availability Factor (EAF), enforce stringent NERC CIP and ERCOT compliance, and ensure seamless power delivery from commissioning through long-term operations. Partnering closely with Engineering, Technical Services, Asset Management, Origination and Trading, executive leadership, the Transmission Service Provider, and local authorities, you will set the operational standard for one of the most technically ambitious power campuses in the country. 
 
Team overview
 
This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Operations team ensures that our utility-scale generation, storage, and high-voltage assets perform safely, efficiently, and reliably at scale—combining deep technical judgment, data-driven decision-making, and disciplined field execution to maximize uptime across the fleet. Joining this team means leading the most complex multi-technology campus in our portfolio from construction handoff into long-term operation, shaping how dedicated clean energy and flexible thermal infrastructure power modern computing while growing alongside collaborative industry leaders.
 
What you'll do
 
Lead Campus Strategy and Multi-Technology Orchestration
Provide overarching operational leadership across co-located solar PV, wind, BESS, and fast-start reciprocating gas assets, aligning technology-specific targets into a unified campus strategy.
Manage, mentor, and evaluate the Wind, Solar, BESS, Gas, and High Voltage / Substation Site Managers, establishing standardized governance, work practices, and reporting cadences across all disciplines.
Optimize campus-wide Capex and Opex through shared logistics, collective spare parts management, cross-utilization of labor and tooling, and disciplined financial workflows in Stampli and SideTracker.
 
Command High-Voltage Infrastructure, Interconnection, and Microgrid Readiness
Oversee safe, continuous operation of the 345kV/34.5kV breaker-and-a-half switching station and 35kV collector pathways, owning switching, clearance, and outage coordination across generation and behind-the-meter load.
Maintain continuous readiness of the 300 MW BESS and 300 MW reciprocating gas microgrid for islanded operation, overseeing grid-forming inverter controls, black start capability, transition/resynchronization procedures, and periodic verification testing.
Serve as the primary on-site interface with the Transmission Service Provider, balancing authority, and ERCOT scheduling coordinators while enforcing flawless NERC CIP and ERCOT reliability standard compliance.
 
Drive Cross-Technology Performance, Dispatch, and Commissioning Handoff
Partner with Origination and Trading and the Operations Control Center to optimize real-time dispatch across variable clean energy, BESS state of charge, and fast-start gas to meet rigid power factor, market, and behind-the-meter data center commitments.
Direct preventative maintenance programs engineered for Texas Panhandle environmental extremes—including ~40°F diurnal temperature swings, dust mitigation, and high-lightning/surge exposure—while leading root cause analysis with Technical Services.
Lead construction-to-operations handoff across all technologies, including commissioning validation, punch list closure, staffing execution, and executive briefings synthesized via SCADA/EMS, G Suite, Lucidchart, Claude, and Gemini.
 
Champion Safety, Regulatory Compliance, and Community Stewardship
Enforce a zero-harm safety culture under OSHA Title 29 protocols, standardizing LOTO, high-voltage switching, arc flash procedures, and incident command across battery thermal, gas, wind rescue, and severe weather hazard profiles.
Manage local regulatory and community obligations in Gray County, including Chapter 312 tax abatement compliance, wildlife mitigation plans, and county road agreements.
 
What you'll bring
 
Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical En

jobs.title: Operations Associate, University District, #13
jobs.description:
Gopuff is looking for Operations Associates (OAs) to join the operations team. Directly reporting to a Site Leader, OAs play an essential role at Gopuff that requires drive, perseverance, positivity, and enthusiasm for the challenge. You will accomplish a variety of operations responsibilities including picking, packing, receiving product both within our site and accompanying kitchen (if applicable), and working with our partner drivers.

Customers turn to Gopuff to provide their everyday essentials—day and night, rain or shine. We're assembling a team of thinkers, dreamers and risk takers who are ready to help us reshape the world of retail faster than ever before. And it doesn't hurt if you like snacks.


Responsibilities: 
-Pick and pack items for dispatch to customers
-Receive and unpack pallets of product from vendors, ensure physical inventory count matches purchase order/invoice, and resolve discrepancies
-Manage inventory and re-shelving of canceled orders
-Clean and organize sales floor and overall facility
-Manage waste and spoilage through strict compliance with FIFO practice
-Contact customer for substituted or out-of-stock items
-Handle, scan and move product in a safe and well-organized manner
-Stand, push, pull, squat, bend, reach and walk during shifts
-Use carts, pallet jacks, dollies and other equipment to move product
-Handle products that may contain tobacco, nicotine, and/or alcohol
-Work in freezer locations periodically throughout shifts
-Capability to walk several flights of steps periodically throughout the day
-Prepare quality beverages and food menu items for all customers by observing all recipes and presentation standards
-Ensure accuracy of all food and beverage packaged for delivery
-Follow health, safety and sanitation guidelines for all products
-Receive and put away order/invoice, and resolve discrepancies when they do not match expiration requirements
-Maintain Kitchen Facility organization and standards to ensure resources can be accessed while managing waste and spoilage through mindful pouring and food preparation
-Prepare, package and stage/handoff orders

Qualifications:
-High School Diploma or GED Equivalent
-Experience working in a restaurant or retail environment (preferred, not required)
-The ability to work a fluid schedule and be available during peak shifts (1st, 2nd, 3rd shifts)
-General working knowledge of basic web-based software applications (e.g. Google G-Suite)
-Stand and walk for the duration of an assigned shift
-Lift up to 49 pounds
-Available to work flexible hours that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, nights and holidays

jobs.title: Roots Internship Program
jobs.description:
A BIT ABOUT YOU
Understanding, people-oriented, and helpful, you feel rewarded by being of service to others. You clearly have a passion for the natural world and are curious how you can build your career in concert with it. The highlight of your day is spending time outdoors, and it’s even better when you’re doing it with friends. You’re in your Sophomore year of pursuing a Horticulture degree and eager to learn where your degree can take you and all the different ways you can make a difference.  
 
A BIT ABOUT US
We like plants, people, and beautiful spaces. John Mulhall came to Omaha in 1953 to landscape, and now, three generations later, we’re as committed as we’ve ever been to making Omaha a more beautiful place to live. Today we’re a team of a few hundred people, but our focus remains the same: working together to engage our community and share our passion for the beauty of the natural world. And we have fun doing it.
 
A DAY IN THE LIFE
As a part of our Roots Internship Program, you’ll report to the People team. You’ll spend time in each of our three Business Units, getting a complete picture of where your Horticulture degree could take you. By the end of the summer, it’ll be clear which part of the business was your favorite, and you’ll have the opportunity to showcase all you’ve learned in a presentation to our leadership team.
 
YOUR IMPACT
o   A rotation with Garden + Home learning about our store experience, plant maintenance, our pro process, our digital brand, and more
o   A rotation with Farms, learning about proper watering, product availability, production plans, and more
o   A rotation with Landscape learning about property enhancement, onboarding new clients, our dependability, and more
o   Create and deliver a capstone presentation on all you’ve learned
o   Contribute to the growth and impact of Mulhall’s and its connection with the community 
 
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
o   A Horticulture student entering their junior year
o   A belief in what we do here: making our community a more beautiful place
o   A reliable people-person committed to maintaining a positive attendance record
o   A communicative team player willing to jump in and assist with a variety of tasks as needed
o   An ability to bend, lift, and work at an active pace
o   A passion for growing a career in concert with the natural world
 
WHAT WE OFFER
o   An inclusive, passionate, and fun work environment
o   The opportunity to grow your career in concert with the natural world
o   An amazing discount on all the plants and plant things you love

HexCoded (hexcoded.ai) is an AI creative studio — creators and brands use our platform to produce video content end-to-end with AI: films, short dramas, and ad creatives. jobs.title: Internship, Supply Chain Analyst (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
Pivotal is the leader in the emerging market of electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft. We design, develop, and manufacture light eVTOL aircraft and are renowned for the BlackFly aircraft the world's first light eVTOL to fly manned missions and enter the consumer market.

jobs.title: FP&A Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
At Neighbor, we’re building the largest hyperlocal marketplace the world has ever seen. We’ve raised over $75 million from top-tier investors such as Andreessen Horowitz and the CEOs of DoorDash, StockX, and Uber. Our marketplace is already flourishing in all 50 states and we’re just getting started!
About the Role
As our FP&A Intern, you’ll work on the numbers leadership uses to run the company. You’ll help build the annual plan, quarterly forecasts, and long-range models, and you’ll present your work to our senior leadership team. You’ll report to the FP&A Manager and work on the real plan, the real forecasts, and the materials that go in front of our board.
Neighbor is a two-sided marketplace, which makes the finance work here unusually interesting. You’ll dig into how supply and demand grow market by market, what drives our take rate, and what it costs to acquire a host or a renter. By the end of the summer, you’ll own expense forecasting for the entire business. 
This internship is a direct path to a full-time role. Strong performers leave with a full-time offer to join the team after graduation.

jobs.description:

About the Role
As our Marketing Operations Intern, you’ll help scale one of Neighbor’s most important growth channels: Google Maps. This role is highly execution-focused and will involve setting up, managing, and optimizing Google Maps pins at scale in partnership with Neighbor hosts.
This is a part-time internship of approximately 20 hours per week.

jobs.title: Technical Program Management Intern
jobs.description:
Our Mission
As humans, there are few things more exciting than meeting someone new. At Tinder, we’re inspired by the challenge of keeping the magic of human connection alive. With tens of millions of users, hundreds of millions of downloads, 2+ billion swipes per day, 20+ million matches per day, and a presence in 190+ countries, our reach is expansive—and rapidly growing. 
We work together to solve complex problems. Behind the simplicity of every match, we think deeply about human relationships, behavioral science, network economics, AI and ML, online and real-world safety, cultural nuances, loneliness, love, sex, and more.

Our Values
Take the Lead: We don't ghost our work or each other. Just as users don't leave their matches hanging, we don't let each other down.
Move Fast: We have a bias for action and urgency. Something that could be done tomorrow would be better if done today.
Better Together: We keep connection at the heart of dating and at the heart of how we work. Just as our users are better when they connect with others, so are we when we collaborate.
Real Talk: We say the hard thing the human way. Just as we ask our users to behave with kindness and candor in our community, we expect Team Tinder to do the same.
Safety First: We act with integrity, transparency, and consistency so people feel safe—whether they're swiping, matching, or working alongside us.
Spark Fun: We have fun to unlock creativity, fuel innovation, and help us build better experiences for daters.


Program Duration
The internship program will run from June 1 through August 31, 2027.
 
Where you’ll work
This is a hybrid role that requires in-office collaboration three days per week in Los Angeles, California. 
 
About the Role 
As a Program Management Intern, you'll spend 12 weeks on the Program Management team owning a real piece of work, not a side project. You'll help keep Product, Design, and Engineering moving in the same direction on projects that ship to Tinder members, and you'll learn how a high-visibility roadmap gets planned, tracked, and delivered.

jobs.title: Strada Education Foundation Internship: Impact Investments Intern
jobs.description:
Are you currently enrolled in a postsecondary education program (an education or training program after completing a diploma or GED)?  Are you eager to make a meaningful impact in communities across the nation and gain practical experience at the same time? Join Strada Education Foundation's summer internship program and be part of a national philanthropic organization focused on better connecting education after high school to meaningful employment and economic opportunity in the U.S.
 
Impact Investments Intern:
As an Impact Investments Intern, you will help Strada invest in organizations working to remove barriers to postsecondary education and workforce pathways, improving socioeconomic mobility for more people. We do that through direct equity in mission-aligned companies and flexible loans to organizations building toward sustainability. Working with the Impact Investments team, you will help refine our impact investing strategy and implement new systems and processes to expand our small team's capacity. You will play an active role in our sourcing, screening, diligence, investment, monitoring, and impact assessment processes. 
 
About Strada
Strada Education Foundation is a national nonprofit social impact organization that supports programs, policies, and organizations that strengthen connections between education and employment in the U.S., with a special focus on helping those who have faced the greatest challenges securing economic opportunity through postsecondary education or training (PSET). Our strategic plan focuses on five focus areas: clear outcomes, quality coaching, affordable PSET, work-based learning, and employer alignment.
Strada works with partners in education and training, nonprofit organizations, industry, startups, and public policy. We leverage strategic philanthropy, investments, research, communications, advocacy, and collaborating organizations as tools to help advance equitable pathways to opportunity. Strada aspires to be a nonprofit partner of choice working with education and training providers and leaders, policymakers, and peer organizations. Strada offers a dynamic, collaborative, and inspiring professional environment that provides learning and professional development opportunities, both within the organization and with external partners.
 
Internship Overview:
Duration: May 18, 2027 - August 13, 2027
Hours: Minimum of 30 hours per week (seasonal employee)
Pay: $22.75/hour undergrad; $25/hour grad
Location: (Hybrid) Washington, DC (in-office on Tuesdays, department-specific days, and other days as needed for special events)
Travel: Up to 15% for Professional Development
 
Program Experience
The Strada summer internship program offers a paid, 13-week, hands-on learning experience for students who are at least one year post-high school. This opportunity is ideal for those seeking to gain experience in social impact while engaging in meaningful functional work. As part of this cohort-based program, interns will gain exposure to nonprofit operations, engage with leadership, and build a network that spans both nonprofit and for-profit sectors. Interns will work on impactful projects, participate in skill-building activities, and attend professional development events such as speaker series and informational interviews.
The internship program will run from May 18, 2027, to August 13, 2027. Interns must be based in the Washington, D.C., area and available for the entire duration of the program. Interns will work in the office at least two days per week (Tuesdays and one additional department-specific day). Additional in-office days may be required for professional development workshops and special events. There may also be opportunities to travel to conferences and workshops during the program.

jobs.description:
The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early!


About National Taxpayers Union Foundation
National Taxpayers Union Foundation is a non-partisan research and education organization dedicated to showing Americans how taxes, government spending, and regulations affect them. Through data collection, analysis, and commentary, we empower citizens to engage in the critical policy debates of our time and hold elected officials accountable. To educate our target audiences, we perform incisive research and analysis on a wide range of policy issues with a particular focus on tax, technology, interstate commerce, legislative scoring, and trade. General Information
Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, PLF battles for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion.
 
As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California; Arlington, Virginia; and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. Interns work remotely by default, but they can request to work physically in any of PLF’s offices. This is a part-time role.
 
You: An inquisitive, creative, and self-motivated college junior, senior, grad student, or recent graduate who knows the principles of liberty and seeks to advance them. You have strong written and oral communication skills and enjoy problem solving.
 
Them: Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources.
 
Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation (PLF) is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the US Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 20 cases heard by the Court. PLF also has nearly 200 active cases across the nation. At PLF, we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game.
 
The Strategic Research intern will be a member of the Strategic Research team. This team produces high-quality social science research to support PLF’s mission-driven goals. The team coordinates with PLF’s Litigation, Legal Policy, Constitutional Scholarship, and Communications teams. This internship is an opportunity for a wide variety of experiences, including the following:
 
·      Communicating with public officials to obtain public records.
·      Collecting, organizing, and analyzing data using Microsoft Excel, R, Python, GIS, or Stata.
·      Conducting literature reviews on such topics as regulatory reform, housing supply, property rights, coastal land rights, and more.
·      Developing internal data for litigation, communications, or legal policy campaigns.
·      Writing blog posts, op-eds, or one-pagers on topics relevant to PLF’s work.
 
 
How to Apply
If you think you might be a good fit, submit the following application materials in ONE PDF when you upload yourrésumé that includes relevant experience in the liberty movement and professional skills:
·      A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants.
·      A writing sample.
·      A semester schedule (if taking classes during the internship period).

jobs.title: Finance and Accounting Intern
jobs.description: About Andercore   Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.  Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.  We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.  We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.  Where we are today:    Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers    Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond    80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai    $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW    The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.     What you will do     Assist in the preparation of financial statements, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements.      Support financial analysis efforts by gathering and analyzing financial data to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement.    Help maintain accurate financial records and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and accounting standards.    Support the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions by processing invoices, payments, and receipts.    Assist in the preparation of tax filings and compliance activities, including gathering supporting documentation and completing forms.    Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Growth, Operations, Tech) to support financial projects and initiatives as needed.        Who you are     Currently enrolled (or recently graduated) in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.    Excellent English and German skills    Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data and draw meaningful insights.    Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other financial analysis tools.    Knowledge of accounting principles and practices.    Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.    Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.    Proactive attitude and willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment.      We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.

You'll support month-end close, help keep the books accurate, and get exposure to how accounts payable, accounts receivable, reconciliations, and reporting actually work at a fast-growing company — not just the theory from a textbook.  This is a hands-on role for someone who wants real reps on the fundamentals: journal entries, reconciliations, and the discipline of making sure every number ties out. Use AI tools to streamline manual, repetitive accounting tasks and help automate reconciliations.    Help develop and enhance our monthly reporting processes, making them faster and more reliable. Foundational understanding of accounting principles (debits and credits, basic GAAP concepts) from coursework.    Strong attention to detail and a low tolerance for numbers that don't tie out. jobs.title: Finance Operations Intern (m/f/d)
jobs.description: Über Buena   Buena digitalisiert die Hausverwaltung in Deutschland. Wir übernehmen traditionelle Hausverwaltungen und transformieren sie in moderne, technologiegetriebene Unternehmen – mit dem Ziel, Immobilienverwaltung einfach und transparent zu machen.   Deine Rolle   In deiner Rolle als Praktikant im Bereich Finance Operations bildest du das verlässliche Rückgrat unseres Finanzteams. Du steuerst die kompletten Abläufe der Kreditorenbuchhaltung, begleitest aktiv die Einführung frischer Systeme sowie Abläufe und agierst als maßgebliche Schnittstelle zu externen Steuerberatern. Gleichzeitig garantierst du reibungslose, strukturierte Prozesse in unseren Tochterunternehmen. An der Seite von Finance Lead und CFO erhältst du umfassende Einblicke in sämtliche Finanzstrukturen, vom einzelnen Beleg bis zur strategischen Liquiditätssteuerung.   Was du tun wirst      Accounts Payable:  Du managst unseren Eingangsrechnungs-Workflow von A bis Z – Postkorb, Invoice Chasing, Freigabeprozesse und Zahlungen ausführen. Sorgfalt und ein Auge für Details sind hier entscheidend.     Buchungsqualität:  Du stellst sicher, dass Rechnungen mit den richtigen Konten, Kostenstellen und Steuersätzen erfasst werden. Du bist die erste Instanz, bevor Buchungen zu unseren Steuerberatern gehen, und unterstützt bei buchhalterischen Rückfragen.     Tochtergesellschaften:  Du überprüfst regelmäßig die BWAs unserer Töchter, erkennst Abweichungen und Unplausibilitäten und stellst sicher, dass vorgegebene Prozesse konsequent eingehalten werden.     Liquiditätssteuerung & Systemimplementierung:  Du erlernst die Arbeit mit Agicap – unserem zentralen Werkzeug für Eingangs- und Ausgangsrechnungen, Zahlungsabläufe sowie das Liquiditätsmanagement. Zudem begleitest du den Rollout in unseren Tochtergesellschaften, schulst die Teams vor Ort und gewährleistest eine hohe Datenqualität und Vollständigkeit.     Ad-hoc & Ops-Schnittstelle:  Du packst auch mal an, wenn es brennt. Sei es bei Finance-nahen Sonderprojekten oder gelegentlicher Unterstützung im Ops-Bereich.     Du passt gut zu uns, wenn     Du Ownership liebst und nicht wartest, bis jemand anderes eine Rechnung sucht, einen Fehler korrigiert oder einen Prozess aufräumt – du siehst es, du löst es.    Du Buchungen nicht als lästiges Pflichtprogramm siehst, sondern verstehst, warum die Kontenwahl relevant ist – für das Reporting, für die Steuer, für das große Ganze.    Du dich in einem Tool schnell zurechtfindest, das du vorher noch nie gesehen hast. Agicap, Moss, Lucanet, Datev – wenn du eines davon kennst, lernst du die anderen schnell.    Du in Unklarheit handlungsfähig bleibst. In einem Startup sind Prozesse oft im Aufbau. Du baust mit, anstatt auf fertige Strukturen zu warten.    Du Qualität mit Pragmatismus verbindest. Du machst es richtig – aber du weißt auch, wann „gut genug“ besser ist als „perfekt in drei Wochen“.    Du fließend Deutsch und Englisch sprichst. Die Kommunikation mit unseren Steuerberatern und Tochtergesellschaften erfolgt auf Deutsch, während wir intern auf Englisch kommunizieren.  Hard requirement.     Du aus unserem Office in Prenzlauer Berg arbeiten willst. Das ist keine Remote-Rolle.  Hard requirement.      Was du bekommst     Bis zu €500 Office-Nähe-Bonus, wenn du innerhalb von 10–20 Gehminuten zum Office wohnst (oder hinziehst).    €110/Monat Mittagessen-Budget, €50 monatlicher Fitness-Zuschuss.    €1.200 jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget.    Kostenlose Bücher: Buena zahlt jedes Buch, das du lesen möchtest.

jobs.title: Director of Product, Clasp Student Finance
jobs.description: Location   Open to Remote in EST or CST Locations. Up to 10% travel required.     About Us   Clasp is a mission-driven, venture-backed startup transforming access to education and career pathways. A college education was always meant to lead to economic mobility. But with rising costs and shrinking loan availability, many working-class and first-generation students don’t have the money they need to finish school. That’s where Clasp comes in. We’re the market leader in institutionally funded gap loan programs. We partner with schools to design, launch and manage lending programs that keep students enrolled, graduating and thriving.  Fresh off our Series B, Clasp is entering its next phase of growth. Recent recognition includes:    TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 (Loan-Linked Hiring)    Forbes Fintech 50    Business Insider:  Top 14 Healthcare Startups to Watch in 2026  and  43 Startups to Bet Your Career On in 2025     Our work spans two business lines:  Clasp Talent helps healthcare employers attract and retain critical talent by connecting them with diverse candidates and using student loan repayment as a powerful recruiting and retention tool. We meaningfully connect employers, educational institutions, and learners to drive mutual benefit.  Clasp Student Finance equips colleges and universities with lending technology to launch and operate their own private student loan programs, enabling schools to step in and support their students directly with financial aid. Recent federal financial aid changes are reshaping how institutions think about supporting their students, and Clasp Student Finance is poised to meet this moment. This role is focused solely on Clasp Student Finance. You can learn more about this business line   here  .     Who We Need   We are hiring a Director of Product for the Clasp Student Finance business line. We’ve seen rapid acceleration since recent federal student loan policy changes. We’re landing deals with large, name-brand universities who are seeing that Clasp’s offering is crucial for filling gaps in student loan financing. We have real product market fit, but there is a lot to build when it comes to scale, excellent borrower experience, and the enterprise features that large universities need. We're hiring a Director of Product to make the right calls on our product strategy to make sure we can capitalize on this momentum.  You'll own the product strategy for Clasp Student Finance and work across our executive team, product, engineering, compliance and lending operations to deliver it. We want you to bring your own point of view, back it up with data, and push back when you think we're heading the wrong way. Some days you'll present the year's product plan to our executive team and board. Other days you'll be in refinement with engineering, making the call on a single feature. You'll manage PMs, hire and grow the team, and talk directly with customers.     What You’ll Do     Own the product strategy and roadmap for Clasp Student Finance, co-leading execution alongside the Director of Engineering    Build a repeatable way to onboard and integrate schools, including how they certify loans and how we connect to their student information systems. We need to launch enterprise university customers without custom builds    Decide where we make our product bets – prioritize across student application experience, university customer asks, and platform modernization    Pair deeply with Compliance and bring them in early on every decision. Shipping in a regulated environment requires a strong relationship between Product and Compliance    Represent Clasp's product vision to school partners, at higher-ed finance conferences and inside the company. This isn't a sales role, but you should be able to explain why a school needs what we're building.    Learn our lending platform end to end, from application and disclosures through school certification, data and disbursement with our bank and servicing partners. Become the person everyone goes to with product questions about it.    Become an expert on student loan policy and where Clasp can go to continue to meet the needs of students and universities. You should be deeply passionate about the problem space.     What You’ll Need     7+ years in product management, including recent hands-on work. You're comfortable working across the spectrum from executive strategy to sprint planning.    Experience managing direct reports and building a team: you’ve hired, created an org chart, and coached PMs.    Experience with in-school student loans. You don’t need to have spent your entire career in this space, but we need someone who understands the basic mechanics of financial aid packaging, loan applications, certification and disbursement, and servicing.    Experience partnering with Compliance to balance risk with the Product vision.    The ability to learn a complex system quickly. You need to be able to look at diagrams, API docs, read docs, and then grok a complex system quickly.    Commercial judgment. You connect customer problems to revenue, and you can make a clear tradeoff when schools, students, and internal teams want different things.    You take a position and defend it. You've disagreed with senior leaders, done the research to back up your view, and changed decisions while keeping their trust.    You use AI deeply. You can show us how you’ve automated things to have an impact on teammates, customers, and your own workflows.     Nice to haves:     Experience at a startup or growth-stage company is a plus    Experience at a fintech that works with bank partners, such as a lending-as-a-service is a plus     What We Give In Return     Competitive cash and equity compensation    Health benefits (health, dental, & vision)    Student loan repayment benefits    401k + match    Flexible PTO policy    Opportunities to grow and perform in a fast-paced environment alongside a stellar team     Salary   The salary range for this po

jobs.title: Data Operations Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description: ABOUT CYVL  The best infrastructure is invisible. You only notice it when it fails. For decades, the people responsible for our roads, bridges and sidewalks have been asked to manage the physical world with tools that can't see it.  Cyvl is the Physical AI company changing that. We build purpose-built sensors, computer vision and AI that turn every drive into current data: what exists, where it is and what condition it's in. 500+ cities and towns use our Infrastructure Intelligence Platform to direct the work and fix problems before they fail. 1 in 30 Americans drive on roads managed with Cyvl data.  The proof isn't a dashboard. It's a smoother commute, a safer walk to school and public dollars going where they matter most. We're a fast-moving team in Boston building hardware, software and AI for the real world. If you believe technology's highest calling is public good, come build with us.    THE ROLE  You'll join the Data Operations team, the group that turns raw street-level capture into the map layers 500+ cities rely on. Every day, sensor data from the field flows through our processing pipelines and comes out as road conditions, sidewalk inventories, sign catalogs, and pavement scores. You'll own pieces of that pipeline: running deliveries end to end, catching data problems before a customer does, and writing the scripts that make the next delivery faster than the last.    WHAT YOU'LL DO    Process customer deliveries end to end: run geospatial data through our Python pipelines, validate the output, and publish the final layers to the Cyvl platform.    Build QC checks that review data automatically.    Investigate failed and stalled processing jobs in our AWS pipelines, find the root cause, and document the fix.    Automate recurring manual steps into repeatable scripts and runbooks, and measure the time saved.    Partner with engineering and customer success to turn field-reported issues into code fixes or process improvements.      WHAT YOU BRING    Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field    Proficiency in Python; comfortable writing scripts that read, transform, and validate data    Comfort working in a terminal and with version control    Available full-time for 10-12 weeks in Summer 2027, based in our Somerville office      NICE TO HAVE    GIS experience (QGIS or ArcGIS, and formats like GeoJSON, shapefiles, GeoPackage)    Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, especially AWS    SQL and experience querying real datasets    Exposure to geospatial Python libraries (geopandas, shapely)    Interest in civic infrastructure, transportation, or public-sector technology    A knack for the business side: you think about how data drives decisions and like problems like "how do we track this better" or "how do we make this visible to the team"    Experience building dashboards or turning data into something a non-technical person can act on      WHY CYVL   Hard tech. Real streets. Your name on it.      Hard problems in the real world.  You build end-to-end: our own hardware, software and AI, with work that shows up on the street in the real world.     Ownership that compounds.  You own outcomes, not tasks. You work directly with customers and across our team, and you'll own more, sooner, than almost anywhere else.     Intense, with heart.  We're building a category, so it's not a place to coast. We also take care of each other, have genuine fun together, and believe in what we are doing.      WHAT WE ASK     Cross lanes.  "Not my job" doesn't exist here.     Own without a playbook.  The plan is still being written, often by you.     Try, miss, try again.  We make big bets. Some won't land, and we learn fast.     Be in the room.  We're on-site in Somerville about 90% of the time.    We're a startup building a category. If that sounds like the draw, not the risk, we'd love to talk.    OUR VALUES     Real:  Authentic and transparent. Focused on solving real problems with simple, effective solutions.     All Out:  Bold, driven, and committed to delivering results that matter.     Accelerating:  Always learning, growing, and moving with intention.     Reliable:  We follow through and deliver at a consistently high bar.     Empowering:  We lift each other up and help governments build infrastructure they can be proud of.      SEE OUR WORK     How Atlanta cut downtown potholes by 60%      How Buffalo turned a campaign promise into a paving plan      How to rebuild US infrastructure smarter       WANT TO GO THE EXTRA MILE? (OPTIONAL)  If you're excited about this role and want to tell us more, email dataopsintern@cyvl.ai with the subject line "Data Ops Intern, [Your Name]" and answer any or all of these:    Why Cyvl, and why a startup? What draws you to this kind of work, and to a small team where your work ships right away?    What's the coolest thing you've built with AI? A class project, side project, script, or experiment all count. Tell us what it did and what you learned.    Tell us about a time you solved a problem by fixing the process instead of just working harder. What was slowing you down? What did you change? What happened?    A few honest paragraphs beat an AI-slop essay. Links to code, notebooks, or demos are welcome.     We build for every community, so we hire from all of them.  The best people for this work come from different backgrounds, paths, and places, and many of them don't check every box. If this role excites you, apply anyway. If you need an adjustment to our interview process, tell us and we'll make it work.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations Intern
jobs.description: Crusoe is on a mission  to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.    We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.    We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.    If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.     About This Role:    Crusoe’s marketing team is scaling fast, and Marketing Operations sits behind almost everything it ships: event follow-up, product launches, gated content, credit campaigns and partner programs. As our Marketing Operations Intern, you’ll work directly with the Marketing Operations lead. You’ll help build, QA and run the campaigns and data processes that turn the team’s work into pipeline for a growing sales organization. This is a real seat on the team. Your work will go live in Marketo and Salesforce, and the projects you own will still be in use after you leave.    This role is for someone curious and detail-oriented who likes building things and wants to see how B2B marketing works behind the scenes. You don’t need to know Marketo yet. You do need to be the kind of person who reads ahead, asks good questions and gets excited when a messy dataset finally comes out clean. This is a paid, full-time, 12-week summer internship for 2027, in office in San Francisco or Bellevue.       What You’ll Be Working On:      Campaign builds and QA:  Build and test email programs, landing pages and forms in Marketo for launches, events and nurture emails and then check them before they go out.     Event and lead data:  Clean, normalize and import attendee and lead lists from events and partners into Marketo and Salesforce, so follow-up goes out fast and to the right people.     Data quality:  Find and fix duplicates, missing fields and bad values, and help keep our database clean as volume grows.     Tracking and reporting:  Keep UTMs consistent and help build the reports that show which campaigns drive pipeline.     AI-assisted tooling:  Use AI tools to automate repetitive ops work, such as data cleanup, QA checklists and documentation, and help make the whole team faster.     Process documentation:  Write clear how-tos and runbooks for the processes you learn, so the next person can pick them up quickly.     Capstone project:  Own one meaningful project from scoping to delivery, such as lead scoring analysis, an attribution deep-dive or a tool evaluation, and present the results to marketing leadership at the end of the summer.        What You’ll Bring to the Team:     Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Information Systems, Data/Analytics or a related field, graduating in December 2027 or by Spring 2028.    0–1 years of professional experience. A previous internship, campus role or part-time job involving data, marketing or operations is a plus, but not required.    Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills: lookups, pivot tables, cleaning and reformatting messy data.    Close attention to detail. You catch the broken link or the wrong segment before it ships. jobs.title: Intern Credit Operations & Automation (f/m/x)

Enpal makes this possible with an integrated total solution for decentralized energy—from solar systems and battery storage to wall boxes, smart meters, and heat pumps. At the heart of it all is our AI-powered platform  Enpal.One +, which intelligently connects thousands of systems and efficiently optimizes electricity procurement and feed-in on the energy market.  EFS is a fintech company specialising in the financing of decentralised energy solutions such as photovoltaic systems and heat pumps. As a factoring and leasing company and an independent subsidiary of the Enpal Group, we enable installation companies and project developers to offer simple instalment and financing solutions to their customers.  Our mission is to accelerate the energy transition through accessible and customer-focused financing products.     What you’ll do   As an Intern in Credit Operations & Automation (f/m/x) at Enpal Financial Services (EFS), you will help make our financing and operational processes more efficient, scalable, and intelligent. You will support core operational workflows while contributing to automation and process improvement initiatives across the customer financing journey. Working in a small fintech team of      Credit Operations:  You support the review of financing applications and customer documents.     Document Verification:  You assess land registry extracts, payslips, and other financing-related records.     AI & Automation:  You help automate operational processes using modern AI tools and workflows.     Process Improvement:  You identify optimization opportunities and help make our operations more scalable.     Cross-Functional Collaboration:  You work closely with teams across Operations, Finance, Commercial, and Product.     Ownership:  You take responsibility for your own projects and actively contribute new ideas.     What you’ll bring     You are currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree, or have recently graduated.    You have already completed at least one relevant internship, working student position, or practical project experience.    You are interested in operations, finance, process optimization, and technology-driven business models.    You enjoy working with AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or similar technologies, and are excited about using them to automate business processes.    You have intermediate  German skills (at least B2 level)  to comfortably understand and review German-language documents.    You communicate confidently in English. jobs.title: Lab Operations Intern
jobs.description: About Etched   Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across prefill and decode. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, we're redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.     Job Summary   Etched's lab keeps our hardware running 24/7. Our chips, modules, and racks are constantly being tested, and we need sharp, reliable hands to make it happen. You'll run test stations, assemble and rework hardware, cable racks, manage inventory, and own the day-to-day operations that turn raw silicon into working systems. You will see how a frontier AI chip goes from a tray of parts to a running rack, and reliable, curious interns take on engineering work over time.    This role is for people genuinely excited about what we're building and willing to do real, often repetitive work with precision and care. Evening and weekend availability is a plus. This role is fully in-person in San Jose.     You may be a good fit if you:     Have extreme attention to detail    Interested in both software and hardware    Are excited about learning how a hardware company works end to end    Are comfortable with hands-on work    Have evening or weekend availability    Curiosity and bias to action — see what needs doing and figure it out       Strong candidates may also have:     Experience with software, mechanical engineering, or thermal systems    Understanding of accelerator hardware, or datacenter environments    Have owned or built hardware testing systems    We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification.     Program details     12-week paid internship     Generous housing support for those relocating    Daily lunch and dinner in our office    Based at our office in San Jose, CA    Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers    Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time      For any questions, contact internships@etched.com     How we're different   Etched believes in the   Bitter Lesson  . We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference.    We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.description: DeFi Quant Trader Intern (Credit)      Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York.     We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.     We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.    We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.     About the Internship Program   Our internship programme gives early-career talent the opportunity to build practical skills, contribute to meaningful projects and learn alongside experienced colleagues in digital finance.  Typically lasting six months and based in our Brussels office (London possible), each internship includes hands-on experience, clear learning goals and dedicated guidance and regular feedback. We look for curiosity, relevant foundational skills, deep, active interest and passion for digital assets and the potential to grow exponentially with us - you don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Where performance, business needs and available opportunities align, an internship may lead to a permanent role, though this is not guaranteed.  We are looking for 3-4 high-caliber Quantitative Analyst Interns to sit within our Strategic Market Making (HFT), Credit and Corporate Development desks/teams (see other openings on our career page for details).   Application deadline: 30 November 2026 Start date: 1 March 2027  Selection process:    Interview with Talent Acquisition representative    Interview with Hiring Manager    Recruitment Challenge       The role    About Credit Desk      In our Credit & On-Chain Liquidity team, we design strategies and deploy capital across decentralized lending protocols, managed vaults, and credit facilities. Operating at the intersection of quantitative finance and smart contract technolgy, the Credit Desk is responsible for optimizing yield, evaluating counterparty and protocol risk, and deploying programmatic credit solutions across digital asset markets. As a Credit Desk DeFi Quant Trader Intern, you will work directly with quant traders and credit strategists to build quantitative risk models, automate yield harvesting, analyze on-chain liquidity pools, and evaluate DeFi protocol mechanics.     Key Responsibilities of a DeFi Quant Trader intern in this unit     On-Chain Risk & Credit Modeling:  Develop and refine quantitative risk models to assess protocol health, collateralization ratios, liquidation risks, and smart contract vulnerability exposure across DeFi credit platforms.     Yield Optimization & Execution:  Build Python-based tools and algorithmic models to analyze real-time yield curves, liquidity pool depth, and funding rate arbitrage across lending and borrowing protocols.     Data Analytics & Monitoring:  Query on-chain data, EVM event logs, and lending protocol data using SQL, Subgraphs, and Python to generate actionable insights for credit positioning and risk allocation.     Protocol Due Diligence & Forensics:  Perform quantitative forensics and stress testing on emerging lending primitives, liquid staking protocols, and structured credit products prior to capital deployment.      Who You Are/Key Requirements     Technical & Quantitative Skills:  Strong code-first foundation in Python, familiarity with Rust with Solidity as a plus. Understanding of smart contract mechanics and DeFi primitive mathemtaics (including propAMMs, lending pool utilization curves, liquidation thresholds).     Quantitative & Trading Mindset:  Rigorous background in a quantitative field (Math, Physics, CS, Finance, or Engineering) with a systematic/trading mindset. Ability to model yield dynamics, credit risk, backtesting strategies, and protocol insolvency scenarios.     DeFi “Skin in the Game”:  Hands-on experience interacting with decentralized lending protocols (e.g., Aave, Morpho, Compound, Maker/Endgame), yield aggregators, or credit markets.     Nice-to-Haves:  Familiarity with Rust, Solidity, Foundry, or specialized credit risk models and backtesting frameworks. Autonomy & Impact - our flat structure means you can contribute your ideas from day one and help shape the foundation that will power Keyrock’s future business.    Culture of Excellence - we value nimbleness, drive for success, owner mentality and collaboration.    Opportunity to leave your mark and start your career  in one of the most reputable  companies in the digital assets world    We are envisioning for the internship to be based pre-dominantly in Brussels. It is possible for a selected candidate to be based in London, UK, provided at least 1-2 months onboarding period would be spent in Brussels together with the rest of the interns cohort.        Our recruitment philosophy   We value self-awareness and powerful communication skills in our recruitment process. We seek fiercely passionate people who understand themselves and their career goals. We're after those with the right skills and a conscious choice to join our field. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who’s driven, collaborative, acts with owners

As a Quantitative Analyst Intern within the HFT track, you will work alongside quantitative researchers, traders and engineers to analyse market and trading data, test hypotheses through backtesting and simulation, and build tools that improve strategy performance and risk visibility. Build and validate latency-aware, event-driven backtests with explicit assumptions around maker/taker execution, queue position, fill probability, fees and cancellations. Build reusable Python tools and data pipelines using modern columnar analysis and SQL for strategy research, performance attribution and monitoring. Execution awareness: You can reason about the order lifecycle from signal to acknowledgement and fill, including exchange APIs, latency, queue position, partial fills, cancellations, fees, slippage and adverse selection.    Digital asset markets: You understand key differences between spot and perpetual futures, including basis, funding, leverage, liquidation risk, settlement currencies and residual exposure.    Quantitative reasoning: You are comfortable with probability, statistics, time-series analysis and evaluating noisy results without overstating significance. jobs.title: Summer Intern - Commercial
jobs.description: WHO WE ARE  Kunin Technologies is revolutionizing the critical mineral supply chain by implementing advanced separation technologies to capture value from overlooked resources.  Metals are everywhere, in solar panels, smartphones, electric vehicles, but as ore grades plummet globally, traditional extraction methods are failing. China dominates critical minerals markets by developing superior separation technologies that extract value from materials American mines discard as waste.  Utilizing Kunin Technologies' breakthrough mass manufacturable nano-separation systems, significantly more value can be produced from each resource, reducing waste, and unlocking metal abundance.  To achieve metal abundance, humanity must bring separation science down its own Moore’s Law: fix the idiot cost index for micro and nano scale separation materials. This requires mass manufacturing novel ion-exchange media form factors which previously struggled from high costs.  THE ROLE  Kunin sells recovery of critical metals from resources that are discarded today: mine tailings, process liquors, industrial by-product streams and low-grade ores. Every commercial conversation starts with a question of economics: what is in the resource, what does it cost to recover, and what is it worth. You spend the summer answering that question for real resources and real counterparties.  You work on the commercial team directly with the CEO. You build the pipeline of candidate resources, chase down samples from mines, refiners and industrial partners, and turn assay data and process assumptions into cost and value models that decide which projects Kunin pursues. By the end of the summer we expect a resource database with samples in hand for the priority targets, and a process cost model per target that the team uses in partner negotiations.  RESPONSIBILITIES    Resource sourcing: identify and screen mines, tailings facilities, refineries and industrial waste streams carrying target metals, and maintain the resource database.    Sample collection: contact resource owners, arrange sample shipments and site visits, and log chain of custody and assay results.    Financial modeling: build project cash-flow models (capital cost, operating cost, revenue, sensitivities) for candidate resources.    Process cost modeling: estimate reagent, energy, labor and equipment costs per metric ton of feed and per kilogram of metal recovered, working with the engineering team on mass balances.    Prepare one-page project summaries and briefing materials for partner and customer meetings.    QUALIFICATIONS AND PREFERRED SKILLS    Undergraduate or graduate student in mining engineering, metallurgy, chemical engineering, economics, finance or a related field, graduating 2027 or 2028.    Modeler skilled in Excel; comfortable with mass balances and unit conversions.    Comfortable cold-contacting mine operators, refiners and industrial partners to secure samples and data.    Exposure to mineral processing, hydrometallurgy or commodity markets preferred.    Ability to work in fast paced and demanding atmosphere.    Self-driven contributor who closes loops without being asked and writes clearly.    ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS    Position located in Chattanooga, Tennessee for the summer of 2027 (approximately 12 weeks, start date flexible).    Occasional domestic travel for site visits and sample collection.    Extended hours during critical project phases.    Strong performers will be considered for a full-time position at Kunin upon graduation.    Chattanooga is more beautiful than expected, and Tennessee has no income tax.   "The Whole World Is Ion-Exchange And The Rest Are Merely Details!"   Dr. Robert Kunin of Rohm and Haas, The Pioneer of the Ion-Exchange Industry, 1951

jobs.title: Operations Internship (MBA / Upperclassman)
jobs.description: About the Company   LightTable is an AI-powered construction document review platform built for preconstruction teams that was just named one of Fast Company's Next Big Things in Tech for 2026. We automate cross-document conflict detection across the complex, multi-party workflows that define how data centers and large commercial projects are designed and built. We recently closed our Series A led by Innovation Endeavors and are in active enterprise deployments with some of the largest GCs and developers in the country.  We move fast, we care about leverage, and we build with AI. We do this not just for our customers, but internally too. You'll find a hard working team that will give you an incredible opportunity to quickly grow in your career.   About the Role   A Series A company that is winning enterprise deployments has to run like one. Over the next year, the way LightTable manages its money, its data, its customer delivery, and its people has to become as rigorous as the product we sell. That is what this role is for.  As our MBA Associate, you will work directly with the Chief of Staff & CEO as a force multiplier across the business: building the systems, processes, and reporting that let a small team operate with the discipline of a much larger one. One week you might be rebuilding our budget-versus-actuals model; the next, cleaning up pipeline data in HubSpot, documenting a customer onboarding playbook, or pulling evidence for our SOC 2 audit. The common thread is that you leave every function more measurable, more repeatable, and less dependent on any one person's memory.  This is a hands-on, high-exposure seat. You will see how a venture-backed company actually runs at the founder level, and you will own real outcomes rather than shadow them. We will refine the role together as we learn what the business needs most.   What You'll Do      Finance and FP&A.  Support the monthly close, maintain budget-versus-actuals and cash forecasting, keep billing and revenue recognition clean as contracts grow, and help prepare board and investor reporting with our CFO consultant.     Systems and process.  Own the health of our internal systems, starting with our ERP: data quality, pipeline hygiene, and the dashboards leadership uses to run the business. Write the SOPs and playbooks that turn tribal knowledge into something the whole team can run.     Customer operations.  Partner with our Engagement Managers/delivery team to build the operating layer behind customer delivery: onboarding trackers, usage and health metrics, and documented implementation playbooks that make each new account faster than the last.     People and admin operations.  Help run employee onboarding, keep our policies and handbook current, manage vendors and renewals, and gather evidence for compliance work such as our SOC 2 Type II audit.     Force multiplier for the CEO/Chief of Staff.  Expand the bandwidth of the CEO and Chief of Staff, by taking on a mix of high-priority and lower-priority tasks with speed, discretion, and judgment about what matters.     Special projects.  Take on market and competitive research, FP&A deep dives, and other strategic or ad hoc work as the business needs it, often using AI tools to get there faster.     What We're Looking For      Current MBA student (or exceptional upperclassman)  able to work in person 2 to 3 days a week in our Denver office (15 to 30 hours per week). Exceptional upperclassmen (juniors and seniors) with relevant finance, consulting, or operations experience are also encouraged to apply.     Analytical rigor.  You are fluent in spreadsheets and financial models, and you care about getting the number right. Experience in finance, consulting, operations, or an analytical role before business school is a strong plus.     Systems thinking.  You see the process behind the task. When something is done by hand twice, your instinct is to document it, automate it, or build the dashboard that makes it visible.     AI-native approach.  You already use AI tools to work faster and you are curious about where they can replace manual work. You think in systems before you think in headcount.     High ownership and sound judgment.  You take a loosely defined problem, figure out what good looks like, and see it through without waiting for direction. You are comfortable with ambiguity and know when to ask.     Influence without authority.  You can work across a company, get busy people to follow a process, and manage up and sideways with tact.     Speed, confidentiality, and a bias for action.  You will handle sensitive financial, people, and customer information and move quickly without being careless.     Very fast learner and hard worker.  You pick up new domains, tools, and context quickly, and you like being busy.     Nice to Have     Hands-on experience with HubSpot, QuickBooks or similar accounting tools, or BI and dashboarding tools.    Exposure to SOC 2 or other compliance programs.    Experience working at or building within an early-stage startup.    Experience in or adjacent to the construction industry.     Why Join LightTable AI?     Learn how a venture-backed company actually runs, working directly with the Chief of Staff and alongside experienced founders and world-class engineers.    Own real outcomes across finance, systems, customer delivery, and people at a company in active deployment with some of the largest GCs and data center builders in the country. jobs.title: Intern, Enterprise Growth & Strategic Accounts
jobs.description: About Parspec   Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to identify products that best meet their needs—instantly. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction.  Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world’s oldest and largest industries.     The Opportunity   How do you turn a successful first deployment into an enterprise-wide relationship? That question sits at the heart of this internship.    We are looking for an intern to work alongside Parspec's sales leadership on one of the most important commercial questions we have: how do we build a repeatable expansion playbook for our largest customers? Our biggest accounts, national distributors and rep agencies, rarely start big. They begin with a single team, branch, or workflow. The ones that grow into enterprise relationships follow patterns we have only partially mapped. Your job is to find those patterns, turn them into account strategy, and prove that strategy on live deals. You will also help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, from the commercial economics to the deal terms.   This is not a shadowing role. You will own a defined body of work with a concrete deliverable, present your findings directly to leadership, and watch your analysis get applied to active proposals while you are still here. If you see yourself heading toward go-to-market leadership, a startup operating role, or founding a company someday, this is a chance to learn enterprise growth by actually doing it, with real stakes. First-year MBA students will find the scope and the executive exposure especially well suited to a summer between years.    What You Will Achieve and Key Responsibilities    Find the growth pattern     Analyze how our major distributor accounts expanded from their first deployment into additional workflows, branches, and business units    Figure out what made the successful expansions work, and what stalled the ones that didn't, using product usage data, deal history, and conversations with sales leadership and customers    Segment our installed base by expansion potential, separating accounts with real headroom from the ones that are already fully penetrated    Help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, working through the commercial economics, the value exchange for both sides, an      Build the account strategy     Develop expansion plans for priority distributor and rep agency accounts, including sequencing, stakeholder mapping, and entry points for each new workflow    Quantify what each additional workflow is worth, both for the customer (time saved, hit rate, revenue capture) and for Parspec (ARR, retention, account durability)    Build the business case materials our sales leadership uses in executive-level customer conversations      Put it into practice     Apply your analysis to live expansion proposals during your internship, working directly with the CEO and sales leadership on deal strategy    Help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, working through the commercial economics, the value exchange for both sides, an    Deliver a documented expansion playbook covering account selection, value quantification, stakeholder strategy, and proposal templates that the sales team keeps running after your internship ends    Present your findings and recommendations to Parspec's leadership team      Why This Matters   Parspec's growth increasingly depends not just on winning new logos but on deepening relationships with the customers who already trust us. Expansion revenue is the most capital-efficient growth a SaaS company has, and in a space as relationship-driven as construction distribution, the companies that systematize expansion win the category. Today, much of this knowledge lives in a few people's heads. This role turns it into a durable, repeatable system, and the playbook you build will outlast your internship.    Who You Are   You are a highly motivated student with strong analytical skills and genuine commercial instinct. You are just as comfortable in a spreadsheet as you are in a customer conversation. You form hypotheses quickly, test them against data, and communicate with the clarity that executive audiences expect. Ambiguity does not slow you down. You structure the problem, make the call, and adjust as you learn.    Mandatory Qualifications     Currently pursuing a degree (undergraduate or graduate) in Business, Economics, Management Science, Finance, Data Analytics, or a related field    Strong analytical and modeling skills, including comfort building customer economics and business cases from incomplete data    Structured problem-solving ability: you can break an ambiguous question down into an answerable workplan    Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the presence to work directly with a CEO and customer-facing leaders    A real ownership mentality: you have taken something from question to shipped result without being managed through it      Preferred Experience     First-year MBA students strongly preferred    Prior professional experience in consulting, banking, revenue or business operations, enterprise sales, or a startup operating role    Exposure to B2B SaaS business models, enterprise or key-account selling, or customer success economics    Experience with CRM systems (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce) and BI or analytics tools    Interest in construction, building materials, industrial distribution, or vertical SaaS businesses    Experience in fast-pac

jobs.title: Sales Operations Intern
jobs.description: As a Sales Operations Intern (m/w/d), you will keep the engine behind our sales teams running cleanly: you own recurring CRM hygiene, accurate user set-up and reliable bonus data so reps can spend their time selling. Supporting the Head of Sales Operations and the GTM Engineer, you will work across a global, multi-market and two-tier sales organisation, partnering with Sales Leads, Customer Service and the Data team to turn messy inputs into decisions people can trust. From your first month you take real ownership of the processes that keep user management, bonus calculations and reporting accurate.  PERGOLUX designs and sells premium, Scandinavian-inspired outdoor living products, from aluminium pergolas to awnings and garden furniture, direct to consumers. We are a company that has grown consistently across Europe and beyond, with around 300 employees, 9-figure revenue and operations across our core markets, and Sales Operations sits at the centre of how that growth is planned, measured and paid.   What You'll Do   - Onboard and offboard sales users across HubSpot, Aircall and our messaging tools (seats, permissions, teams and task queues), keep the set-up aligned to the org chart, and run a monthly seat and licence check.  - Prepare the monthly data for bonus calculations for Sales Leads, Tier 2 reps and the Tier 1 partner, check inputs against source data (orders, attribution, owner changes, returns), and flag exceptions before payout.  - Run recurring CRM hygiene programmes (duplicates, missing or wrong fields, wrong owners, stale deals and tasks, inactive workflows), track data quality per market, and follow up with Sales Leads where logging standards slip.  - Pull and prepare weekly and monthly sales reports from HubSpot, Looker and spreadsheets, and answer ad hoc questions such as conversion by market, speed to lead, task backlog or rep activity.  - Support the GTM Engineer with data checks and analysis for capacity planning and productivity projects, and act as first point of contact when reps are stuck with access or tool issues.   What You'll Bring   - Enrolled or recently graduated with Bachelor's or Master's degree in business, economics, information systems, data or a related field.  - Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivots, clean formulas) and an eye for numbers that do not add up.  - Structured and reliable: you finish recurring tasks on time, every time, and document what you do.  - Fluent English.  - Nice to have: first experience with a CRM (HubSpot or Salesforce) or a BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Power BI), basic SQL, German or another market language, and an interest in sales, operations and AI tools.   💼 Compensation  — Competitive salary · Company pension plan · Capped overtime, fully paid, no endless unpaid crunch   🚀 Growth and Career Development  — You get real ownership of recurring processes from the start with direct impact on how a multi-market sales organisation is run, you learn hands-on HubSpot administration, CRM data governance, Looker reporting and how incentive schemes are designed and tested, and you work alongside an international, collaborative team with fast-track opportunities to grow as PERGOLUX scales.   ⏰ Time Off and Flexibility  — Up to 30 vacation days, starting at 27 · One week per year remote workation in the EU/UK   🌟 Benefits and Lifestyle   - Jobrad / Bike leasing programme, promoting sustainable and healthy commuting  - Regular team events (summer party, Christmas party, after-work gatherings) and retreats  - Modern setup and laptops (Apple or Windows)  - Employee discounts on PERGOLUX products  📍  Office Location  – Schlesische Str. 27 C, 10997 Berlin, Building C, 6th floor (hybrid)   How to Apply   Ready to keep our sales engine clean and accurate? Apply through our [Career Page]( https://pergolux.careers/ ) or reach out via [LinkedIn]( https://www.linkedin.com/company/pergolux/posts/?feedView=all ). This is a 6-month, full-time internship (part-time from 30 hours per week is possible), based in Berlin on a hybrid basis.  PERGOLUX is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, we think it's less about ticking every box and more about what you bring to the table!

You’ll work directly with the founding team to research prospects, pick up the phone, send thoughtful gifts, and turn creative outreach into real conversations. One day, you might put together a personalized package for a supply chain executive. The next, you’ll call them, learn about their challenges, and book a meeting.
