jobs.title: Undergraduate Investment Analyst Intern (Summer 2027) - Investment Office
jobs.description: Reporting to the Managing Director of the Investment Office, this Undergraduate Investment Analyst Intern role at Carnegie Mellon University is an exciting opportunity for a motivated and current student, who is interested in gaining broad-based investment analysis and portfolio reporting experience in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.  The right candidate will be someone who is incredibly detailed and comfortable with day-to-day analytical work, but who can also think creatively, research new investment opportunities, and generate innovative ideas in support of the University’s investment objectives. This person must also be confident in their ability to effectively communicate and present those thoughts and ideas to senior leadership.  Carnegie Mellon’s goal is to become a leader in endowment management, overseeing a comprehensive global portfolio invested with premier managers across major asset classes, including public equities, hedge funds, private equity, venture capital, real estate, natural resources, distressed opportunities, and fixed income.  Working closely with Carnegie Mellon’s Investment Office staff, the successful candidate will play a key supporting role in the management and oversight of the University’s endowment and other long-term financial investments.     The Investment Analyst Intern’s responsibilities will focus on supporting the investment staff in the following areas:   Managing the development of systems and models for monitoring the investment portfolio  Conducting extensive due diligence, both qualitative and quantitative, on various investment managers  Preparing presentations for the University’s senior administration and Investment Committee  Performing research on new and existing investment strategies and market opportunities, as appropriate     You should demonstrate:    Familiarity and utilization of Microsoft Office products  Excellent written and verbal communication skills  Ability to work effectively both on an independent basis and within a collaborative team environment  Outstanding interpersonal, listening, and presentation skills  Knowledge of investment management concepts and current global events and market conditions    Adaptability, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. We are in search of a team member who can effectively interact with a varied population of internal and external partners at a high level of integrity. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work.    Qualifications:    Must be currently enrolled as an undergraduate student (Sophomore) with a major in Real Estate, Consulting, Mathematics, Statistics, Accounting, Business Administration & Management, Business Analytics, Economics, Entrepreneurship, Finance & Financial Management, or International Business.  GPA: 3.25 minimum     Additional Information:    This is a fixed term position, approximately 12 weeks, expected to work during the summer of 2027   Work Posture:  This position is operating in-office presence of 5 days a week, (Greater Pittsburgh region based) near our Pittsburgh, PA campus   Sponsorship : Applicants for this position must be currently legally authorized to work for CMU in the United States. CMU will not sponsor or take over the sponsorship of an employment visa for this opportunity.  Carnegie Mellon is not a qualifying employer for the STEM OPT benefit: only the 12-month OPT may be used to work at Carnegie Mellon.  To be considered for this position, please submit your resume along with a cover letter.           Joining the CMU team opens the door to an array of exceptional benefits.       Benefits eligible  employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including   comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance     as well as a generous   retirement savings program   with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with   tuition benefits  , take well-deserved breaks with ample   paid time off   and observed   holidays  , and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.       Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our   Family Concierge Team   to help navigate childcare needs,   fitness center access   ,  and much more!      For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our   Benefits page   .       At Carnegie Mellon, we value the whole package when extending offers of employment. Beyond credentials, we evaluate the role and responsibilities, your valuable work experience, and the knowledge gained through education and training. We appreciate your unique skills and the perspective you bring. Your journey with us is about more than just a job; it’s about finding the perfect fit for your professional growth and personal aspirations. jobs.description: Job Details     New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.    Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.      As an Academic Part Time Intern, you will be a member of the Business Administration Team and will report to the Business Manager.    Responsibilities :  The JPL Acquisition Division has an exciting business part-time internship opportunity for an undergraduate studying Business Administration, or a related major. This intern will have the opportunity to gain hands-on work experience in the application of subcontracts within Financial and Business Operations, to include issuing and managing active non complex and moderately complex subcontracts, purchase orders, and agreements; close-out of inactive subcontracts and agreements; providing support to the subcontract managers in the handling of complex, high-dollar subcontracts.    Responsibilities include:    Provide support to subcontract managers in developing and issuing solicitations for goods and services.    Prepares documentation appropriate to the value of the subcontracts and necessary to satisfy internal audit and review requirements.    Responsible for communication necessary to convey significant activities associated with the issuance of low dollar subcontracts internally and externally.    Performs activities necessary to ensure the goods and services purchased are received in accordance with the price and delivery schedule and that closeout activities are handled promptly.    Performs standard transactions that update the financial business process/systems based on departmental instructions.    Works on day-to-day assignments under direct supervision; receives detailed instructions on new assignments.    Uses applicable policies, procedures and practices as guides to determine work methods and deliver results.    Seeks guidance in applying applicable policies, procedures and practices to new situations to determine appropriate action.    Interacts primarily with immediate supervisor and team members within own organization.    Participates on a team within own organization.      Required Qualifications          Must be currently enrolled at least half-time at an accredited college or university pursuing a Bachelors degree in Business or related discipline.    Must be able to work a minimum of 20 hours per week, with a maximum of 30 hours per week while in school.    Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work in a team environment.    Minimum GPA 3.0/4.0.      Desired Qualifications      Completed coursework with exposure to standard principles, theories, concepts and techniques in business communications and database spreadsheets.    Prior internship experience in related business areas.    Ability to rapidly comprehend and apply subcontracting principles in high-volume environment    Participation in student organizations.    Intermediate to advanced knowledge of MS Excel, Word and PowerPoint.    Ability to interface with all levels of personnel and the ability to resolve multifaceted issues.    Punctual, details oriented, resourceful and a self-motivated individual.      The hiring range displayed below is specifically for those who will work in or reside in the location listed. In extending an offer, Jet Propulsion Laboratory considers factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s job related skills, experience, knowledge, and relevant education/training.         The typical hourly rate for this job in Pasadena, California depending on education level is $21.00 as a freshman, $22.50 as a sophomore, $24.50 as a junior, and $26.50 as a Senior.          JPL has a catalog of benefits and perks that span from the traditional to the unique. This includes a variety of health, dental, vision, wellbeing, and retirement plans, paid time off, learning, rideshare, childcare, flexible schedule, parental leave and many more. Our focus is on work-life balance, and living healthy, fulfilling lives as we Dare Mighty Things Together. jobs.title: Internal Audit Intern 2027 - REMOTE
jobs.description: Job Details    CNO Financial Group, Inc. (NYSE: CNO) is a leading insurance and financial services company focused on securing the future of middle‑income America. Through brands such as Bankers Life, Colonial Penn, and Washington National, CNO delivers life and health insurance, annuities, financial services, and workforce benefits to more than 3.3 million policyholders, supported by $38.3 billion in total assets.    With a strong financial foundation, national presence, and a culture rooted in integrity, excellence, and people‑first values, CNO offers meaningful opportunities for professional growth and impact across its U.S. locations, including its headquarters in Carmel, Indiana.    To be eligible for consideration, candidates must currently possess unrestricted authorization to work in the United States.  Please note that the Company does not intend to sponsor work visas with respect to this position or future full-time employment opportunities.    This is a paid internship, at competitive rates.  The Memorial Day and 4th of July holidays are paid days off.    CNO Financial Group is hiring Internal Audit Interns to work alongside our Internal Audit associates, assisting with professional day-to-day work in the department.     Core responsibilities and deliverables:     Complete Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) testing for assigned business process controls under the supervision of a lead.   Document SOX testing work clearly and accurately, including procedures performed, evidence reviewed, sample selections, testing results, and conclusions in accordance with Internal Audit methodology.  Collaborate with Internal Audit team members and business process owners to request evidence, clarify documentation, follow up on open items, and resolve questions identified during testing.          What you need (Minimum requirements):    Progress towards a bachelor’s degree in accounting or related discipline.  Status as a rising junior or rising senior, approx. graduation dates of December 2027-June 2029.  Availability to work 40 hrs/week for 10-12 weeks during the summer.  Foundational experience with Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Excel.  Ability to communicate professionally (written and verbally) across all levels inside and outside of the organization.  Candidate location in Central or Eastern US time zone is preferred OR willingness to work Central or Eastern time zone business hours.      What will set you apart (Preferred experience):    Prior internship experience.  Balancing education and a part time job during the school year.  Participation with university clubs. Practical GIS and data visualization skills suited to developing dashboards and integrating information from multiple sources.      A strong interest in, or relevant experience of, climate change and climate change adaptation.      The ability to communicate technical information clearly through written and audiovisual materials.      Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to work independently within an agreed workplan.      A collaborative approach and willingness to work with colleagues across different countries and contexts.      An interest in environmental stewardship and creation care within Compassion’s ministry. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-plus-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, advisory, and consulting groups as well as our enabling services functions. That’s why we continually invest in innovation, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.     Job Description:    What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe  Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.    As you grow, you’ll also begin to take ownership of client relationships, contribute to account strategy, and support the delivery of high-impact work. Developing a sense of account leadership, including understanding client needs, ensuring delivery excellence, and building trusted partnerships, is part of what sets successful consultants apart.    Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.    As a  Finance and Compliance team  member in  Crowe’s Consulting Practice  your role will be focused on helping clients resolve business needs in the areas of accounting and finance. You will have the opportunity to work on diverse teams with experienced experts to problem-solve and present constructive solutions to our clients. At Crowe, we empower you to take risks, to challenge yourself in specialized areas of consulting & technology, and to generate solutions that impact the firm and your professional growth. Crowe cultivates a creative company culture where you will have the opportunity to share your ideas and knowledge with clients from your very first day with the firm.      You will assist Public Sector clients with navigating the financial and capital markets, developing strategies for funding various projects, and completing long-term capital and operational planning. Typical projects in this role include budget assistance (both revenue and expenditure estimation), bond market research, financial modeling, revenue analysis, assistance preparing utility rate and fee studies, attendance at public meetings; participation in client meetings; and assistance preparing analyses for economic development projects.       Additional roles are focused on the following areas:     Accounting Consulting (Financial reporting, accounting standard implementation, finding mitigation)     Compliance (Attestation engagements, incurred cost audits, GAGAS performance audits, grant compliance consulting, subrecipient monitoring, indirect cost compliance)     Internal Audit (Audits, co-source internal audit, outsourced internal audit, risk assessment, internal control assessment, Enterprise Risk Management)        Skills and Requirements:       Gather and Review Financial & Compliance Documentation     Collects financial statements, policies, procedure manuals, and other relevant materials for initial assessment     Verify that required documentation aligns with applicable standards (e.g., GAAP, IFRS, basic regulatory guidelines)     Conduct Basic Compliance Testing     Follows standardized testing procedures to assess adherence to internal controls or regulatory requirements (e.g., SOX controls, anti-money laundering checks)     Tracks and documents any identified exceptions or non-compliant activities     Prepare & Organize Workpapers     Maintains thorough and accurate workpapers (physical or electronic) detailing testing samples, results, and initial observations     Ensures the traceability of findings according to firm or industry standards     Support Engagement Execution     Assists in data entry, reconciliations, or preliminary analyses under guidance from senior team members     Contributes to engagement administrative tasks such as scheduling, file management, and updates to project trackers     Exhibit strong verbal and written communication skills when consulting with senior management, C-suite client personnel, and government regulators. Apply business writing skills to produce high-quality, client-ready deliverables     Demonstrate strong critical thinking skills to solve complex problems, generate practical solutions, and contribute to strategic outcomes     Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments. Adapt to changing priorities and risk landscapes while managing time effectively     Show a desire to continuously learn and build a deeply specialized skill set that evolves with industry demands     Cultivate strong relationships with clients, colleagues, and the community to support collaboration and long-term success     Possess the ability to quickly acquire new skills, tools, and concepts with a mindset focused on ongoing personal and professional development     Apply systematic, analytical approaches to problem-solving and interpreting complex data sets and regulatory requirements     Self-motivated to deliver high-quality results, take responsibility for outcomes, and grow through feedback and experience

jobs.title: Workday Student Senior Principal Consultant, Records & Admissions
jobs.description: Join Cognizant's Workday Student Practice in Australia and New Zealand and help universities transform how they manage the student journey, from first enquiry through to completion. As a Senior Principal Consultant, you'll lead design and configuration across Student Records, including academic structure, enrolment, progression, completion and government reporting, and extend that expertise into Recruiting and Admissions, including prospect management, applications, Tertiary Admissions Centre processes and offers. You'll guide institutions on how Workday Student can best meet their needs and support their strategic goals, lead workstreams and mentor other consultants. This is a real opportunity to grow your career while helping shape how the sector operates.    This role suits a senior practitioner with a background in student records, student administration, admissions or student systems who wants to turn their knowledge of student lifecycle regulations and processes, and their commitment to supporting students, into a consulting career. You'll bring higher education and regulatory expertise to every engagement, working closely with student administration, admissions, future students, international and technology teams. You'll be equally comfortable in functional design sessions and integration discussions, making sure your designs align with Student Financials, Academic Advising, external systems and other areas of the Workday platform.      Key Responsibilities      Lead discovery and design sessions for academic structure, student records, enrolment, unit and course changes, progression, leave of absence, withdrawal, completion and graduation.      Lead Admissions design across Tertiary Admissions Centre (TAC) and direct entry channels, including the pathway and alternative entry routes used by international students, transfer and non-traditional applicants, covering application processing, assessment, offers, acceptances and deferrals.      Configure Student Records and Admissions business processes, rules, eligibility, holds and statuses.      Design the end-to-end handling of Tertiary Admissions Centre (TAC) applications, preferences, offer rounds and responses, and align and collaborate with integrations and technical teams on the full solution.      Work with client teams to define how regional CRMs used for student recruitment interact with Workday Student, including the hand-off of prospect and applicant data.      Define requirements that bridge functional design and integrations, including data mapping, triggers, timing, error handling and ownership, and work closely with integration teams through build and testing.      Bring an understanding of how Australian or New Zealand universities manage student records to design discussions, so Workday Student is configured for local course structures, terminology, policy settings and reporting obligations.      Ensure designs capture the data and processes needed for TCSI reporting, Unique Student Identifier (USI) requirements, international student obligations including PRISMS and Confirmations of Enrolment, and related compliance needs.      Work with Student Financials and finance stakeholders to align the financial impacts of admission, enrolment, changes, withdrawal and completion events.      Identify data, security, privacy, records management and reporting requirements across the student lifecycle.      Document requirements, design decisions and configuration.      Prepare and execute unit testing, support end to end and integration testing and assist with defect resolution.      Support data conversion of historical student records, cutover preparation, training and go live readiness.      Provide clear advice on Workday leading practices while recognising institutional context and policy obligations.      Lead workstreams, coach and review the work of other consultants, and act as a trusted advisor to client process owners.      Contribute reusable configuration guidance, test assets and delivery methods to the Cognizant Student Practice.       Experience we are looking for      Senior experience in student records, student administration, admissions, student systems or a related higher education function.      Understanding of academic structure, enrolment, progression, completion and graduation processes, and how they are reflected in student records.      Familiarity with Tertiary Admissions Centre processes, such as those run by UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC or TISC, including application preferences, offer rounds and data exchange with institutions.      Familiarity with CRMs commonly used for student recruitment in the region, such as Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365, and how they connect to a student information system.      Working knowledge of TCSI reporting, including how student, course and enrolment data is captured, validated and corrected.      Familiarity with the regulations that relate to student records in Australia or New Zealand, such as the Higher Education Support Act, the ESOS Act and National Code, the Higher Education Standards Framework, USI requirements, privacy and state records legislation, or the Education and Training Act and Single Data Return.      Ability to work with requirements that bridge functional and integration design, and to communicate confidently with both business and technical teams.      Proven experience guiding business stakeholders through key operational and policy decisions, including presenting options, explaining trade-offs and securing agreement.      Experience implementing, supporting or serving as a super-user for student information systems (SIS), with Workday Student experience highly regarded.      Experience leading a workstream or team and mentoring other consultants or practitioners.      Experience facilitating workshops, documenting decisions and working across student administration, admissions, international and technology teams preferred.      Experienc

jobs.title: Workday Student Financials Consultant
jobs.description: Join Cognizant's Workday Student Practice in Australia and New Zealand and help universities transform how they manage student finances. Working directly with clients on Workday Student deployments, you'll lead design and configuration across tuition and fee assessment, billing, payments, sponsorships, refunds and reconciliation. Your role goes beyond working out how Workday Student can meet a university's needs. You'll help them use it to support their strategic goals, from improving the student experience to strengthening financial sustainability and compliance. This is a real opportunity to grow your career while helping shape how the sector operates.    This role suits someone with a background in student accounts, university finance or student administration who wants to turn their knowledge of student financial regulations and processes, and their commitment to supporting students, into a consulting career. You'll bring higher education and student finance expertise to every engagement, working closely with finance teams, student administration and student services, and making sure your designs align with Student Records, Workday Financial Management and other areas of the Workday platform.        Key Responsibilities      Lead discovery and design sessions for tuition and fee assessment, student billing, payments, payment plans, sponsorships, refunds and receivables.      Configure Student Financials business processes, rules, charge structures, due dates and accounting related requirements.      Design practical handling for waivers, adjustments, reversals, third party arrangements and exceptional cases.      Configure student account processes in alignment with institutional policy, financial controls and regulatory requirements.      Work with Student Records and finance stakeholders to align the financial impacts of enrolment, changes, withdrawal and completion events.      Document requirements, design decisions and configuration.      Apply your higher education experience to shape practical future-state processes for student finance and student administration teams.      Bring an understanding of how Australian or New Zealand universities manage student fees and finances to design discussions, including Commonwealth supported places, HELP loans, the eCAF process and Commonwealth Assistance Notice, so Workday Student is configured for local fee structures, funding arrangements, terminology and policy settings.      Identify data, security, reporting and integration requirements, including payment gateways, banking and finance platforms.      Define reconciliation, operational reporting and audit requirements for student financial activity.      Prepare and execute unit testing, support end to end testing and assist with defect resolution.      Support data conversion validation, opening balance activities, cutover preparation, training and go live readiness.      Provide clear advice on Workday leading practices while recognising institutional context and policy obligations.      Contribute reusable configuration guidance, test assets and delivery methods to the Cognizant Student Practice.       Experience we are looking for         Experience in student accounts, student fees, university finance, receivables or a related higher education finance function.      Understanding of tuition and fee assessment, billing, payments, refunds, sponsorships and reconciliation.      Working knowledge of Commonwealth supported places and HELP loans, including student contribution amounts, HELP eligibility and census date rules, and how they flow through fee assessment, student accounts and government reporting.      Familiarity with the regulatory context for student fees and finance in Australia or New Zealand, such as HELP arrangements under the Higher Education Support Act, TCSI reporting and ESOS National Code refund requirements, or Fees Free and StudyLink arrangements.      Proven experience guiding business stakeholders through key operational and policy decisions, including presenting options, explaining trade-offs and securing agreement.      Experience implementing, supporting or serving as a super-user for student information systems (SIS) or enterprise finance systems.      Ability to translate financial policy and operational requirements into structured system design.      Experience facilitating workshops, documenting decisions and working across finance, student administration and technology teams preferred.      Experience with testing, financial validation, data conversion, training or deployment readiness activities preferred.         About the Cognizant Workday Student Practice        The Cognizant Workday Student Practice is focused exclusively on helping universities across Australia and New Zealand transform the way they support students, faculty and administrators throughout the student lifecycle.    What makes our practice different is the combination of higher education practitioners and Workday specialists working together. Many of our consultants have worked inside universities as academic services professionals before moving into consulting. That experience allows us to bring practical insight into the operational, regulatory and policy considerations that shape solution design.    We work with institutions to design and implement sustainable Workday Student solutions that support local regulatory requirements, align to institutional strategy and remain adaptable as university needs evolve. Our goal is not simply to deploy technology, but to help universities establish a foundation they can continue to own, operate and enhance long after implementation is complete.    #LI-Remote       Why choose Cognizant:     Entrepreneurial environment that welcomes your ideas  Opportunity to do great work  Outreach programs that support communities and tap into your volunteer spirit  Learning opportunities to help current needs and advancement   Global operations, with op

jobs.title: Director of Campus Operations (2026-2027 School Year) [Immediate Start]
jobs.description: POSITION: Director of Campus Operations (DCO)  GRADE LEVEL: Middle School and High School (Grades 6–12)  LOCATION: Multiple DSST Public Schools locations across Denver and Aurora, Colorado.  View current openings.  We encourage you to apply even if your preferred location is not yet listed.  SALARY: $77,500–$92,500 based on up to 10 years of aligned experience. We also offer a relocation stipend for candidates moving from 75 miles or more outside Denver!  STATUS: Full-time, year-round, benefits-eligible, exempt, in-person position  START: Immediate Winter 2026-27  View the school-year calendar.     Lead the Operations That Make Exceptional Schools Possible!   At DSST Public Schools, we believe exceptional school operations create the foundation for outstanding teaching and learning. We're looking for organized, solutions-oriented leaders who love developing people, building effective systems, and creating school environments where students and educators can thrive.   As a Director of Campus Operations (DCO), you'll oversee the non-instructional operations of a DSST campus, typically serving both middle and high school students. You'll lead the Front Office team, manage critical school systems, and serve as a strategic partner to the School Director as a member of the School Administration Team.   Why Join DSST as a Director of Campus Operations?   Make a Schoolwide Impact: Lead the systems that create a safe, welcoming, and well-organized environment for students, families, and staff. By participating in our paid intern program, you’ll develop industry-related knowledge, enhance skills that are transferable to any professional setting and do meaningful work to help achieve our goals. Your daily responsibilities, special projects and activities will provide both structured and unstructured opportunities to help you learn and grow as a professional. When you network with executives, connect with a mentor, explore other departments and volunteer in the community, you’ll see your impact at EMC on a larger level. Plus, successful interns are invited to apply for regular full-time positions. Join us at EMC! You’re going to love it here—you can count on it.         **This position is eligible to work a hybrid (3 days in office/week) schedule from the    Cranston, RI area   **     Essential Functions:    Summer paid internship working in one of EMC’s branch underwriting departments  Assists underwriters in obtaining information needed to properly evaluate new business and renewal submissions, including correspondence with agents and other outside sources  Learns EMC culture, business processes and products  Gains an understanding of the insurance underwriting process     Education & Experience:    Business major, preferably in insurance, marketing or finance  Completion of junior year preferred  Interest in property casualty insurance career  Cumulative GPA of 3.00 or higher     Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:    Excellent verbal and written communication skills  Analytical ability  Strong organizational skills  Sound decision-making and problem-solving  Attention to detail  Good personal computer knowledge necessary to analyze and underwrite risks               Our employment practices are in accordance with the laws that prohibit discrimination due to race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, religion, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, active military status, citizenship status, marital status or any other consideration made unlawful by federal, state, or local laws.        All of our locations are tobacco free including in company vehicles.

jobs.title: Network Operation Analyst Level 1 Internship (2026/2027 Intake)
Investor Relations & Sustainability Reporting Intern
jobs.description: Other      Internship / Global Electrolux Talent (GET)        Job Description    Investor Relations and Sustainability Reporting Intern – HQ Stockholm, Sweden     This is an internship for an active student with expected graduation from late 2027 or later of related Bachelor or Master programs at Swedish and European universities.    Start date 1 February 2027 – duration 6 months – full time    If you want to help build the home of the future, start your career with us.  At Electrolux Group, our vision is to be the home appliance industry leader in consumer satisfaction by delivering outstanding lifetime experiences with solutions that always get better. We share ideas and collaborate so that together, we can develop solutions that deliver more enjoyable and sustainable living.    About the role:   The Investor Relations and Sustainability Reporting team is responsible for ensuring high-quality, transparent, and compliant sustainability disclosures that meet evolving regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations. As an intern, you will support key strategic initiatives focused on sustainability reporting transformation, regulatory compliance, and process improvement. You will contribute to the adoption of revised sustainability reporting standards and support the development of efficient, scalable reporting processes and tools across the organization. This is an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in sustainability reporting, ESG regulations, project management, stakeholder engagement, and digital process transformation within a global organization.      What you’ll work on:     ESRS 2.0 Adoption and Implementation     Support the transition to updated ESRS reporting requirements through research, documentation, and stakeholder coordination.    Assist with mapping disclosures, collecting reporting data, and maintaining supporting documentation.    Contribute to reporting projects by preparing materials, tracking actions, and supporting collaboration with internal stakeholders and external assurance providers.    Help improve reporting processes and tools to support accurate, compliant, and auditable sustainability disclosures.          Global Reporting Manual and Process Improvement     Support the development of the Global Reporting Manual by documenting reporting requirements, guidance, and best practices.    Assist in creating reporting instructions, templates, and communication materials for stakeholders.    Contribute to process improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities for standardization, simplification, and automation.    Help prepare presentations, reports, and project updates while collaborating with teams across Sustainability, Finance, and Investor Relations.        What you’ll learn:    Global Reporting Manual and Process Improvement  Support the development of the Global Reporting Manual by documenting reporting requirements, guidance, and best practices.  Assist in creating reporting instructions, templates, and communication materials for stakeholders.  Contribute to process improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities for standardization, simplification, and automation.  Help prepare presentations, reports, and project updates while collaborating with teams across Sustainability, Finance, and Investor Relations.  We offer the possibility of hosting a Bachelor or Master thesis project. The topic should be developed in alignment with the people leader of the position and be relevant for Electrolux Group.      Who you are:    Active Bachelor's or Master's student in Sustainability, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related field. Include your Cover Letter when applying.  Remain an active student throughout the entire internship period with expected graduation date from December 2027 or later.  Interested in sustainability reporting, ESG regulations, corporate sustainability, and business transformation.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Comfortable working with data, documentation, and complex regulatory requirements.  Structured, organized, and able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.  Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.  Experience with Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, reporting systems, or data visualization tools is considered an advantage.  Fluent in English (additional languages are a plus)       Please note that Electrolux Group does not provide visa sponsorship for internships. Candidates must already have the legal right to work in Sweden for the full duration of the internship at the time of application. This may include, for example, EU/EEA citizenship, Swedish permanent residence, or a valid Swedish residence and work permit that does not require employer sponsorship. Electrolux Group does not provide visa or relocation support for internships. You must remain an active student throughout the entire internship period with expected graduation date late 2027 or later.       Where you’ll be:   You will be based in Stockholm, our modern global headquarters, with 1200+ colleagues on site. We work in a hybrid setup that gives everyone up to 20% flexibility to work remotely, while boosting creativity and collaboration through regular office presence. The work contract is full-time and limited to 6 months, with monthly compensation of 21,000 SEK for Bachelor students and 22,000 SEK for Master students.   At Electrolux Group, we believe in learning by doing. This internship gives you hands-on experience, meaningful exposure, and a strong foundation for your future career.  Learn more on how to apply and how we interview on our career page:    https://career.electroluxgroup.com/global/en/internship

jobs.title: Intern, Accounting
jobs.description: We have two openings for this internship. The role will work a hybrid schedule in either our Columbus, Ohio or Charleston, West Virginia office and will report to the AVP, Financial Reporting & Investments or the AVP, Finance, Operations and Tax.       This is a full-time summer internship for the 2027 summer and will require someone who can work at least 40 hours per week.  Start and end dates will be based on availability and business need. Must be currently enrolled and have completed at least 60 credit hours with an accredited college or university.      Pay = $18 per hour     Additional Job Description      Encova Insurance has again been recognized as a RISE Elite Top 50 internship program, making this our sixth year in a row! Rising Insurance Star Executives (RISE) is the voice of young professionals who are looking for ways to share their innovative ideas and spread a new message about who the insurance industry is. As an intern at Encova Insurance you will be part of a dynamic, results-driven team and learn to manage real world situations alongside Encova associates. Our successful internship program attracts students from across our region and our diverse opportunities ensure that our interns are provided with a wide range of learning possibilities! If you know a current Encova Insurance associate and would like to apply as a referral, please encourage them to submit your referral information before you submit your application. Our current policies are based on the laws in states in which we are registered for payroll. Our current footprint includes:    Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin.        JOB OBJECTIVE:       This position is an internship within the accounting organization and may have opportunities for exposure to multiple accounting and/or finance teams (including, but not limited to, financial reporting, investments, reinsurance, property & casualty accounting, accounting operations, accounts payable and tax). The objective is to gain valuable experience within a corporate accounting department, develop an understanding of statutory insurance and other accounting disciplines, and assist in the performance of key team tasks and project work aligned with department strategic priorities.     This is a full-time summer internship and will require someone who can work at least 40 hours per week. Start and end dates will be based on availability and business need.        ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:        Assist in daily, monthly, and/or quarterly accounting tasks such as journal entries, report generation and analysis, tax or compliance activities, accounts payable functions, and/or reconciliations. Support the Accounting department with cross-functional project initiatives.       OTHER FUNCTIONS:        Participate in company-wide intern program activites. Provide backup for employees on vacation for short periods. Other duties as assigned.       KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:        Completion of basic accounting courses required with at least 60 credit hours completed prior to the start of the internship  Advanced Microsoft Excel skills required (e.g., ability to create pivot tables, vlookups, additional advanced formulas)  Ability to work independently and demonstrate problem solving skills  Strong verbal and written communication skills         This position has been evaluated   in accordance with   the Americans with Disabilities Act  .    Encova   Insurance makes every effort to   reasonably accommodate   disabilities to   permit   performance of the essential functions and candidates who need such accommodation are encouraged to seek it  .    This description reflects the nature and level of work performed by associates in this position  .    It is not an all-inclusive inventory of duties, responsibilities and qualifications required  .    It provides   an accurate   overview of the work and skills needed to perform this position  .    Because job content may change from time to time,   Encova   Insurance reserves the right to add and/or   delete   functions from this job as it   deems   necessary for business   reasons.               Ready to join our team?  At Encova Insurance, we firmly believe that our associates drive our company’s success by delivering unrivaled service to our customers. With success in mind, we make an ongoing effort to provide an environment that offers challenging, stimulating and financially rewarding opportunities. Join us to discover a work experience where you can learn and grow to your fullest potential.    What you can expect from us   An internship at Encova is a great way to jump-start your career. Our award-winning, structured summer intern program offers:    Competitive compensation    An introduction to the insurance industry through authentic work experiences    Networking opportunities with industry professionals    Flexible start and end dates    Community involvement and volunteer opportunities      Through our collaborative team structure, we find professional and personal growth. jobs.title: EMBL TechDev Internship Programme
jobs.description: Your role      EMBL is among the world’s highest ranked scientific research organisations aimed to explore the secrets of life. EMBL integrates 29 member states and has six research sites in Heidelberg, Barcelona, Grenoble, Hamburg, Cambridge (Hinxton) and Rome. EMBL, in addition to being a centre of excellence in research, has during its 50 year history contributed important technological and engineering advances to support life science research.    EMBL has been at the forefront of numerous engineering and microscopy breakthroughs, significantly advancing imaging technologies and enabling new biological discoveries. Some of the key innovations developed at EMBL include confocal and light-sheet microscopy to enable high resolution biological imaging; cryo-electron tomography improvements for visualizing intracellular macromolecular structures at near-atomic resolution, and synchrotron beamline instrumentation that allow determination of protein structures at atomic resolution.     The   EMBL TechDev Internship Programme   is a scientific visitor scheme designed to provide early-career students/researchers (prior to embarking on a PhD) with a passion for technology and tool development an opportunity to gain hands-on training experience through participation in ongoing cutting-edge projects in this area at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL). The interns will have access to world-leading research laboratories, mentorship from leading scientists, and exposure to interdisciplinary research in the life sciences. It aligns with EMBL’s ongoing research programme  “Molecules to Ecosystems”  that seeks to deepen our understanding of life by examining biological systems across various scales—from individual molecules to entire ecosystems. A major aspect of ongoing efforts at EMBL is to develop the required cutting-edge instrumentation, tools and technologies necessary to undertake such research effectively.    The primary objectives of the programme are to offer technology minded interns:   a well mentored and training focused stay designed to encourage a career path in interdisciplinary scientific research    a practical and immersive experience in a collaborative, international and interdisciplinary research environment    a platform to develop technical and analytical skills through direct involvement in EMBL’s ongoing technology development research projects      You are     a student enrolled in a recognised university pursuing a  Bachelors  or  Masters  degree in engineering, physics, mathematics or computer sciences and related discipline and/or   an unaffiliated recent graduate  with a Bachelor/Master degree from the abovementioned disciplines (a degree completion certificate must be submitted as part of the application)      Contract length:   varies depending on project (see project list on website)     Salary:     discussed with host after successful application      Why join us    Do something meaningful  By choosing a Trainee/Internship at EMBL, you can apply your talent and passion to accelerate science and tackle some of humankind's greatest challenges. Please watch the video below to learn more about EMBL and how our work makes a difference. Whatever your role, you will be contributing towards these challenges.     Campus life & benefits:      Flexible working arrangements  - including hybrid working patterns      Free shuttle bus to and from work  (Hinxton & Heidelberg)     On-site library      Subsidised on-site gym:  Hinxton only     Subsidised on-site cafeteria(s)      Casual dress code       Extensive sports and social club activities  (on campus and remotely)     Family benefits:  On-site nursery and holiday clubs on campus     Accident at work insurance           What else you need to know      Diversity and inclusion:  At EMBL, we strongly believe that inclusive and diverse teams benefit from higher levels of innovation and creative thought. We encourage applications from women, LGBTQ+ & individuals from all nationalities.      How to apply:  To apply please submit a cover letter and a CV through our online system. Applications will close at 23:59 CET on the date shown below. We aim to provide a response within two weeks after the closing date.       Closing Date  .

jobs.title: Campus Operations Manager
jobs.description: Help shape a campus where world-class science can thrive.       EMBL-EBI    is one of the world’s leading centres for biological data and bioinformatics, supporting scientists across the globe. Behind that work is a    campus    environment that enables people to do their best.   As we grow, expand and modernise, we are looking for a Campus Operations Manager to help shape and deliver safe, welcoming, sustainable and efficient workplace services.     Your role     Working closely with the Head of Campus Operations, you will combine strategic planning with operational leadership to ensure our services meet the needs of our people today and support future campus developments.   Your remit will span facilities management, reception, hospitality, catering, workplace experience and space utilisation. You will lead our Facilities and Reception teams, with five direct reports, and build effective partnerships with Wellcome Genome Campus Limited, EMBL colleagues across Europe and external service providers.   You will have the opportunity to:    Help develop and deliver the Campus Operations Strategy, supporting organisational growth and workplace transformation.  Improve workplace services through staff feedback, service reviews, data analysis and clear performance measures.  Shape policies and standards for space utilisation, meeting rooms, access management and the wider workplace.  Strengthen relationships with campus partners and suppliers, setting clear service expectations and monitoring delivery.  Support sustainability objectives through the Green Committee and coordination of agreed actions.  Lead business continuity planning and coordinate incident management preparations, working closely with the Head of Campus Operations and Health & Safety Manager.  Develop your teams through effective delegation, professional development and succession planning.  Represent EMBL-EBI in campus working groups and governance forums, deputising for the Head of Campus Operations where appropriate.     About you    You will be an experienced operational leader who can translate organisational priorities into practical improvements. Comfortable working across a complex organisation, you will bring sound judgement, a collaborative approach and a clear focus on the people who use our services.   You have      A degree or equivalent professional experience in facilities management, workplace management, business management or a related discipline.  Experience leading and developing teams, managing budgets and delivering operational change.  A track record of managing outsourced services and building productive relationships with a range of stakeholders.  Strong operational planning, contract management and continuous improvement skills.  The ability to analyse data and produce clear reports that inform decisions.  Excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, with the confidence to influence senior stakeholders and balance competing priorities.  A commitment to integrity, accountability, respect and fairness.      You may also have     Experience in a scientific, higher education or international environment  Experience in business continuity, hospitality or workplace services.  Relevant IWFM, project management or health and safety qualifications     Make an impact beyond day-to-day operations    This is an opportunity to shape how a leading scientific institute works: developing people, strengthening services and creating an environment that supports international collaboration and discovery.   If you bring a strategic outlook, practical leadership and a commitment to excellent workplace services, we would welcome your application.      Contrac t  length : 3 years, renewable to a maximum of 9 years    Salary:  Grade 6 or 7 depending on experience. Monthly salary from £3,861.91 (grade 6) or £4,395.66 (grade 7) after tax plus generous benefits and financial allowances based on individual circumstances. Excluding 12.99% personal pension and insurance contributions. EMBL-EBI, part of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory, is a worldwide leader in the storage, analysis and dissemination of large biological datasets. We provide the global research community with access to publicly available databases and tools which are crucial for the advancement of healthcare, food security, and biodiversity.     Join a culture of innovation  We are located on the Wellcome Genome Campus, alongside other prominent research and biotech organisations, and surrounded by beautiful Cambridgeshire countryside. This is a highly collaborative and inclusive community where our employees enjoy a relaxed atmosphere. We are committed to ensuring our employees feel valued, supported and empowered to reach their professional potential.  Watch this  video  to see how EMBL-EBI makes an impact. jobs.title: Analyst Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description: What’s Under the Hood     DriveTime Family of Brands is the largest privately owned used car sales finance & servicing company in the nation. Headquartered in Tempe, Arizona and Dallas, Texas, we create opportunities and improve the lives of our customers and our employees by placing a focus on putting the right customer, in the right vehicle, on the right terms and on their path to ownership.    The DriveTime Family of Brands spans across DriveTime, Bridgecrest and SilverRock.  You can find us at the intersection of technology and innovation as we use our proprietary tools and over two decades of industry knowledge to redefine the process of purchasing, financing, and protecting your vehicle.       That’s Nice, But What’s the Job?         This is not a position for which sponsorship will be provided. Individuals with temporary visas or who need sponsorship now or in the future are not eligible for hire at this time.        We are looking for Data Analytics Interns who possess a strong understanding of analytics and data principles for our Summer 2027 internship program. DriveTime Family of Brands is a highly data driven organization with several analytic departments. Our data analytics interns could support one of the following verticals: Credit Risk & Pricing Analytics, Loan Servicing Analytics, Marketing Analytics, Supply Chain Analytics, Retail Analytics and SilverRock Analytics.     A successful candidate should have knowledge of data analysis tools such as SQL, Python, Tableau and Excel. Above all, the candidate should have a passion for uncovering actionable insights from data.     The analytic interns will be responsible for things like:     Conducting data analysis to generate meaningful insights from data sets    Brainstorm ideas and provide creative solutions to challenges in data analysis    Participate in all phases of the analytic lifecycle, from research design, data collection and data processing to model building, deployment, and presentation of results.    Innovate existing products and services while using technologies and data analysis to identify new opportunities to improve customer experience and profitability.    Provide ad hoc analysis and special projects as required.       So what are we looking for?       Killer analytics and reporting abilities.  You’ll need the capability to analyze data and in return, prepare timely reports on your findings.     A mind for the details.  Okay, we know “detail-oriented” is on about every job description – but we really mean it!     Fantastic problem solver.  Your job is not only to find the problem, but more importantly, find the solution.     Agile in a fast-paced environment.  We move, and we move quickly. Thriving in an environment that never stops, is a must.     Intellectual curiosity.  Why? What? How? Do you find yourself always wanting to learn more and broaden your knowledge base? If so, this could be the role for you!     Excellent verbal and written communication skills.  The ability to talk and write with confidence, charisma and competence for a wide variety of audiences including management.       The Specifics.      Bachelors or Master’s student with a graduation date between December 2027 – May 2028    Pursuing a quantitative degree in Analytics, Data Science, Mathematics, Economics, Statistics, Physics, Computer Science or other STEM fields    You have a GPA of 3.5 or higher    Data analysis experience    Working knowledge in SQL, Python, Tableau and Excel    Our internship program is 11 weeks starting May 2027 – August 2027    Internships will be base out of our Home offices in Tempe, AZ and Dallas, TX    You can expect a regular  on-site  schedule; Monday-Friday, 40 hours per week    Relocation not provided for internship       So What About the Perks? Perks matter.     Not Just Coffee Runs.   We’re talking real world experience. You’ll walk away from our internship program with hands-on experience, completed projects, full portfolios, and newly developed skills.   Who Says You Have to Walk Away?  Across both our Tempe, AZ and Dallas, TX offices, over 60% of our interns stay through the fall semester, return the following summer, or are brought on full-time after graduation.   Growth & Development.  You will be mentored by industry professionals, be given guidance along the way, and the tools to be successful.   Philanthropy: Give for Good.  We are proud to be difference makers in our communities. We dedicate time for our Interns to give back with us.   Gratitude is Green.   Out Internship Program is paid, because, well… money matters!       In-House Gym.  We want our employees to be the best versions of themselves. So come early, take a break in your day or finish strong with a workout!   Give Us a Reason (or not), and We’ll Celebrate.   Regardless of whether there is a holiday or not, we are finding ways to kick back and enjoy each other’s company outside of day-to-day work.   Smart-Casual Dress.  Come dressed in jeans (you’ll fit right in with the rest of us).      Anything Else?  Absolutely.     DriveTime Family of Brands is Great Place to Work Certified! And get this: 90% of our rockstar employees say they feel right at home here.  We could spend a lot of time having you read about ALL our awards, but we’ll save time (and practice some humility) just naming a few others; Comparably Awards: Best Company for Diversity, Best Company Culture and Best Company Leadership, oh and don’t forget Phoenix Business Journal Healthiest Employers (okay, we’ll stop there)!    Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of our background and drug screening process. DriveTime is a drug-free, tobacco-free workplace and an Equal Opportunity Employer. Buckle up for plenty of opportunities to grow in a professional, fun, and high-energy environment!

jobs.title: Graduate Intern- Commercial Title Underwriting (Summer 2027)
jobs.description: Who We Are   Join a team that puts its People First! As a member of First American's family of companies, National Commercial Services provides single-point service for simple to multi-property/multi-state national commercial real estate transactions. Since 1889, First American (NYSE: FAF) has held an unwavering belief in its people. They are passionate about what they do, and we are equally passionate about fostering an environment where all feel welcome, supported, and empowered to be innovative and reach their full potential. Our inclusive, people-first culture has earned our company numerous accolades, including being named to the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® list for eleven consecutive years. We have also earned awards as a best place to work for women, diversity and LGBTQ+ employees, and have been included on more than 50 regional best places to work lists. First American will always strive to be a great place to work, for all. For more information, please visit www.careers.firstam.com.       What We Do   The National Commercial Services Underwriting intern will participate in a program designed to provide graduate and law students with meaningful exposure to the title and financial services industry while developing professional, technical, and interpersonal skills. Interns will gain hands-on experience in a corporate environment through meaningful assignments, opportunities to learn from experienced professionals, networking, and other intern-focused activities, all while working under the guidance of their manager or in-house counsel. 2L and 3L law students participating in the Underwriting program will support assignments related to real estate law and may work on a variety of projects, including legal research for underwriters, preparing indemnity letters, and attending seminars.      What You’ll Do    Conduct legal research in support of underwriting decisions  Analyze real estate law issues, including title, lien, foreclosure, and authority matters  Review policy forms, endorsements, and underwriting standards  Participate in underwriting file discussions and risk analysis sessions  Shadow underwriters on active transactions and approval workflows    What You’ll Gain    Practical exposure to Real Estate Law in a corporate underwriting setting  Insight into title insurance policies, endorsements, and coverage analysis  Experience navigating underwriting systems and legal workflow tools  Professional development through executive presentations and networking opportunities  Mentorship from experienced underwriters and in-house legal professionals  A foundational understanding of risk management    What You’ll Bring    Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite applications  Strong legal research and analytical skills  Interest in Mortgage, Real Estate, Financial Services, Title Insurance, or related industries  Ability to solve problems with attention to detail and sound judgment  Professional maturity and strong written and verbal communication skills  A demonstrated commitment to ethics and integrity  Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively  Initiative, productivity, and adaptability in a professional environment  A customer-focused mindset and commitment to representing the Company professionally    Typical Education    Currently enrolled in an accredited Law School  Rising 2L or 3L law student      $30.00-$34.00/hour   This hiring range is a reasonable estimate of the base pay range for this position at the time of posting.  Pay is based on a number of factors which may include job-related knowledge, skills, experience, business requirements and geographic location.      What We Offer   By choice, we don’t simply accept individuality – we embrace it, we support it, and we thrive on it! Our People First culture is inclusive for all employees - not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it's the key to our success. We are proud to foster an authentic and inclusive workplace For All. You are free and encouraged to bring your entire, unique self to work. First American is an equal opportunity employer in every sense of the term.    Based on eligibility, First American offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401k, PTO/paid sick leave and other great benefits like an employee stock purchase plan.

jobs.title: Intern for: Characterization of Advanced Automation Applications on Universal Controller Platform
jobs.description: Job Description Summary              Job Description     Project description:   GridBeats™ is a portfolio of software-defined automation solutions for grid digitalization. The portfolio is designed to enable utilities and industrial customers to ensure a stable, efficient energy supply amidst the growing integration of renewable energy sources and aging infrastructure. Advanced Automation Applications (AAA) are a part of GridBeats™ portfolio that are designed to help grid operators overcome grid complexity and improve control when managing distributed assets for advanced reliability, resiliency & flexibility.  AAA solutions include electrical monitoring and control systems and power management systems for industrial and utility applications, Distributed Energy Resources (DER) integration solutions, Microgrids control and monitoring solutions, Wide Area Monitoring, Protection and Control solutions (WAMPAC), Remedial Action Schemes (RAS) and Energy Management Solutions (EMS) for Datacenter power plants.  AAA solutions run on the GEV Universal Control Platform (UCP) software platform, hosted on a Rugged Substation Automation PC hardware platform. UCP is GE Vernova's edge device platform. It runs the Linux-based EdgeOS, which grew out of GE Digital's Predix Edge. Each application runs as a Docker container on a Docker Swarm.  The performance of the AAA solutions is extremely critical and require rigorous characterization under different operating conditions. The performance needs to be recorded under various conditions like:  ·       simultaneous operation of multiple containers  ·       operation under different communication loads  ·       operation with various protocols  ·       response times of time-critical applications  ·       response times with cybersecurity measures in place  ·       interface with 3rd party applications  Based on the results, recommendations need to be made to tune the UCP features or the Application architecture to achieve the desired performnace   Skills developed:   RTOS and containerization, Application characterization on RTOS, Performance tuning of time-critical applications, Exposure to industry communication protocols, Introduction to Advanced Automation Applications      If contracted in Spain:   Non-national candidates are responsible to know the minimum documentation requirements to be able to be contracted in country: NIE- Social Security Affiliation Number in Spain (NAF) and Bank Account in Spain. They must be in possession of them at the time of start hiring. GE will not sponsor this requirement.            Additional Information              Relocation Assistance Provided:  No

Job Description    The Role:   Join the Cadillac Racing Program Management team as a Business Operations & Cost Optimization Intern supporting trackside and race-event operations. You will audit spend and processes, analyze budget-to-actual performance, and identify cost-cutting opportunities that improve efficiency, cost visibility, and business control without compromising performance, safety, or race readiness.     The Team:   Cadillac Racing competes at the highest levels of global endurance racing, including the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and FIA World Endurance Championship. The Sportscar Program Management team coordinates the people, partners, budgets, and operations required to compete successfully. This role supports that team by strengthening financial discipline, operational efficiency, and measurable cost-reduction initiatives across the program.     What You’ll Do:    Create a program spend baseline by organizing historical and forecasted costs across selected race-event, logistics, purchasing, travel, freight, equipment, hospitality, and operational activities.  Conduct structured audits of processes and transactions to identify cost drivers, duplication, control gaps, compliance issues, and opportunities for improvement.  Review budgets, invoices, purchase orders, forecasts, and actuals; reconcile discrepancies and organize findings into clear, actionable summaries.  Build Excel-based analyses, dashboards, audit tools, and status reports that help Program Management leadership monitor spending, efficiency, and implementation progress.  Quantify potential savings, develop a prioritized cost-reduction pipeline, and support business cases for approved cost-cutting measures.  Present audit findings and recommendations to Program Management leadership, then help track actions, owners, timing, and realized savings through implementation.  Assess inventory-control practices for trackside parts, spares, consumables, and equipment; reconcile records to actual usage and identify opportunities to reduce excess, obsolete, or duplicate inventory.      Required Qualifications:    Currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Data Analytics, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.  Expected to graduate between December 2027 and May 2029.  Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months.  Strong analytical, auditing, problem-solving, and process-improvement skills, with the ability to translate detailed data into practical business recommendations.  Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to organize data, build clear analyses, identify trends, and communicate recommendations effectively.  Excellent communication, presentation, organization, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to work independently and across cross-functional teams.      Preferred Qualifications:    Experience with process auditing, cost accounting, budgeting, variance analysis, procurement controls, Lean or Six Sigma, continuous improvement, or business-case development.  Experience with financial or operational modeling, Power BI, dashboards, data visualization, or other analytical tools.  Experience in automotive, motorsports, manufacturing, supply chain, event operations, or a similarly fast-paced environment.  Experience developing executive-ready recommendations, presenting findings to leaders, or coordinating implementation across cross-functional teams or external partners. jobs.description: Paste here the job description   Internship Opportunity: Investor Relations Advisory Intern    Location:  Brussels  Start Date:  as soon as possible  Duration:  6 months   Are you ready to shape the future of capital markets? We are looking for an  Investor Relations Advisory Intern  to join the  IR Advisory Team  at Euronext Corporate Solutions. The position will be based in  Brussels , and start as soon as possible.    You will primarily be responsible for:    Producing clients’ periodic market updates and listing reports (weekly memos, capital markets overview, read-across) in line with the quality and commitment standards of the Advisory team  Being involved in Investor Relations Advisory initiatives, including content creation and event participation  Supporting the Advisory team’s development efforts by preparing meeting presentations  Assisting in delivering Shareholder Analysis Reports and helping build client relationships across France, Belgium, Norway, the Netherlands and Italy  Analysing local share registers with Shareholders Rights Directive II and completing shareholder analysis reports for listed companies in Europe of all sizes and sectors  Understanding institutional shareholding movements and providing intelligence on investors’ behaviour  Contributing to strategic group projects focused on analysing shareholding structures of major indices in European markets  Support the IR & Advisory Team on deliverables concerning all topics and mandates based on workflow and priorities    Your profile:    Excellent knowledge of Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel (pivot tables, formulas; ideally VBA skills) and ability to use databases such as Bloomberg and Factset  Attention to detail, analytical and problem-solving skills  Interest in technology, equity markets and sustainable finance is an asset  Fluent in English and French. Dutch is a plus  Business school or university degree (market finance)  Previous experience in capital markets or financial communication is a plus    Join a company where market infrastructure is built on innovation — and where every innovation starts with a bold mind asking, “What’s next?”. At Euronext, we believe change is a starting point, not an obstacle. We look for people who see growth opportunities, think long term and want to help shape capital markets for future generations. Working with us means:    Being part of a European, international and diverse team – Collaborate across borders with talented colleagues connected by a shared ambition and purpose.  Learning as you grow – Develop your skills through continuous learning, real responsibilities and flexible career paths that evolve with you.  Having an impact – Contribute to projects that matter, in an agile and dynamic environment where your ideas help drive progress.  Driving sustainability – Play an active role in building transparent, responsible and sustainable capital markets for the long term.  Together, we do not just support markets – we help shape their future.    Apply by submitting a CV in English.   The IR & Advisory team is part of Euronext Corporate Solutions, dedicated to delivering high-quality advisory to listed companies across Europe. We work closely with clients to provide actionable insights, support investor relations strategies and help companies understand their shareholder base and market dynamics. Join us to contribute to impactful projects and develop your expertise in capital markets advisory.     Join Euronext – Shape capital markets for future generations Euronext is the leading European capital market covering the entire capital markets value chain, from listing, trading, clearing, settlement and custody, to solutions for issuers and investors. We operate seven national stock exchanges, handling 25% of European lit equity trading. Our products include equities, FX, ETFs, bonds, derivatives, commodities and indices. Euronext also provides clearing and settlement services through Euronext Clearing and our network of Euronext Securities CSDs.
