jobs.title: 2027 Fund Internship Program (FIP) - Economists
jobs.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World.          Work on real research. In one summer.    The Fund Internship Program (FIP) offers PhD students in economics an outstanding opportunity to contribute to the work of one of the world's leading international financial institutions.   As a Fund intern, you'll apply your economic research skills to real-world policy questions that matter to the IMF's 191 member countries. You'll work alongside experienced IMF economists, gain hands-on research experience, strengthen your analytical skills, and build a professional network in a uniquely international environment. Many interns present their findings to IMF staff, and some see their work published internally.   If you're passionate about macroeconomics, international policy, and research that can make a global impact, the Fund Internship Program could be your next step.    About the Program   Over 10 to 12 weeks, you'll contribute to an individual research or project assignment while working alongside experienced IMF staff at IMF Headquarters in Washington, D.C. The internship provides practical experience, exposure to the IMF's work, and the opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world policy and operational challenges.  To learn more about the Fund Internship Program and hear from previous interns, visit the    Fund Internship Program page    on IMF Careers.    Eligibility   To be considered for the 2027 Fund Internship Program - Economists, you must:   Be within one to two years of completing a PhD in macroeconomics or a related field.  Be enrolled as a student at the time of the internship and return to your academic studies afterward.  Be under the age of 32 when the internship begins in June 2027.  Demonstrate excellent written and spoken English.    Possess strong analytical, quantitative, and computer skills.     Application Requirements   As part of your online application, you must complete the technical questionnaire and upload the following documents:    Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume    Statement of Interest or Cover Letter  explaining your motivation for applying to the IMF   Evidence of current student status and academic performance , including either:  A recent transcript from your current university program, or     A letter from your university confirming active enrollment and recent grades.      Incomplete applications will not be considered. Only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted by a member of the FIP recruitment team. Previous participants in the Fund Internship Program are not eligible and should not reapply.    Frequently Asked Questions   Is the internship paid?  Yes. The Fund Internship Program is a full-time, paid internship requiring 40 hours of work per week.   How long is the internship?  Internships last between 10 and 12 weeks.   When do internships begin?  The start of 2027 internship is June 7, 2027 (ending August 27, 2027).   What visa support does the IMF provide?  If you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or otherwise authorized to work in the United States, you will require a G4 visa. The IMF will provide the documentation needed to support your visa application with U.S. authorities.   Does the IMF provide housing?  No. Interns are responsible for arranging and securing their own housing accommodation. Resources and guidance may be shared with selected interns during the onboarding process.   Will I be notified when my application is received?  Yes. You will receive an automated confirmation after submitting your application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further consideration.   Are there exceptions to the age limit?  The only exception is for time spent in mandatory military service.        Department:      Hiring For:   A09    The IMF is guided by the principle that the employment, classification, promotion, and assignment of staff shall be made without discrimination against any person. We welcome requests for reasonable accommodations for disabilities during the selection process. Information on how to request accommodations will be provided during the application process.

jobs.title: Student Financial Customer Service Analyst
jobs.description: The Talent Acquisition department hires qualified candidates to fill positions which contribute to the overall strategic success of Howard University. Hiring staff “for fit” makes significant contributions to Howard University’s overall mission.        At Howard University, we prioritize well-being and professional growth.         Here is  what we offer:             Health & Wellness:       Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus mental health support        Work-Life Balance:       PTO, paid holidays, flexible work arrangements        Financial Wellness:       Competitive salary, 403(b) with company match             Professional Development:       Ongoing training, tuition reimbursement, and career advancement paths        Additional Perks:        Wellness programs, commuter benefits, and a vibrant company culture              Join Howard University and thrive with us!                         https://hr.howard.edu/benefits-wellness                       BASIC FUNCTIONS:     The Student Financial Customer Service Analyst serves as a trusted financial resource for students and families by delivering exceptional customer service while ensuring accurate student account management and sound fiscal stewardship. This role leverages technology, data, and proactive communication to enhance the student experience, support operational excellence, and protect university revenue.     This is a full-time, fully in-person position based on Howard University's main campus. Regular on-site presence is essential to provide direct student support, collaborate with campus partners, and perform daily operational responsibilities. To support peak enrollment, billing, registration, and other critical university operations, the position may require compensated evening and weekend work as business needs dictate.      SUPERVISORY ACCOUNTABILITY:          N/A          NATURE AND SCOPE:               This role serves as a frontline Student Accounts coordinator, providing clear, accurate, and empathetic financial guidance to students. The coordinator responds to inquiries by phone, email, and in person—including during some nontraditional hours—and conducts detailed account reviews. They collaborate closely with Cashiering, Bursar Systems, Registrar, Auxiliary Services, and Financial Aid to resolve billing discrepancies and ensure accurate account updates. The position requires strong communication, customer service experience, problem-solving skills, and the ability to support adult learners. The coordinator helps students understand charges, deadlines, holds, and financial processes while ensuring issues are resolved efficiently and in alignment with university policies.          PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:            Serve as a primary point of contact for students, responding to financial inquiries via phone, email, in person, and during some nontraditional hours.      Conduct comprehensive student account reviews and identify discrepancies.      Laise with Cashiering, Bursar Systems, Registrar, Auxiliary Services, and Financial Aid to resolve billing issues and ensure accurate updates.      Educate students on billing policies, deadlines, payment options, and the financial implications of academic actions.      Document interactions, maintain accurate case notes, and ensure timely account resolution.      Provide high-quality, empathetic guidance to support student persistence and financial clarity.        CORE COMPETENCIES:              Ability to deliver patient, empathetic, and solution-oriented support.      Identifies issues, interprets account activity, and determines appropriate next steps.      Clear, concise, and professional written and verbal communication across multiple channels.      Works effectively with cross-functional offices to resolve discrepancies and support accurate billing.      Ensures accuracy in account reviews, documentation, and follow-through.      Comfort working in a fast-paced environment and supporting evening or nontraditional service hours.      Ability to understand and communicate institutional billing, financial aid, and registration policies.                 MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:                     Bachelor’s degree preferred; an equivalent combination of education and directly related experience may be considered.      Experience in customer service and/or financial operations, ideally in higher education or a service-focused environment.      Experience supporting adult or nontraditional learners strongly preferred.      Ability and willingness to work evening or nontraditional hours based on program needs.      Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to provide accurate, empathetic guidance.      Demonstrated ability to analyze accounts, problem-solve, and coordinate with multiple campus offices.         Compliance Salary Range Disclosure      Expected Salary Range:  $60,000 - 64,000

Monitoring changes in the  regulatory environment  and assessing their impact on the organization and client operations. Supporting technology-enabled projects from a  business and governance perspective , ensuring alignment with regulatory and operational requirements.  Coordinating with internal audit teams and client stakeholders to support project delivery.   Designing, developing, and testing data and AI  to support audit and risk management use cases, such as:  Test case development, anomaly detection, and continuous auditing.  Risk indicator identification and monitoring.  Control effectiveness testing and trend analysis.    Developing and enhancing  analytics tools and AI prompts/scripts  to automate audit and risk processes.  Leveraging  prominent AI frameworks and libraries  to build, evaluate, and refine models used in audit and risk engagements.  Analyzing differences in policy management, control environment, and governance practices, identifying leading practices across financial institutions.  Monitoring changes in the  regulatory environment  and assessing their impact on audit scope, risk profiles, and compliance requirements.  Supporting updates to the  Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework , including major risk identification and maintenance of risk inventories. Strong conceptual, critical thinking, analytical, professional judgement, and practical problem-solving skills.  Excellent verbal and written communication skills. U.S work authorization is required.

jobs.description: The opportunity    Are you curious about how secure digital banking services are designed, assessed and protected? As an IT Risk and Application Security Intern at ING, you will work alongside security, engineering and risk professionals to identify application-security risks, support remediation and strengthen secure ways of working. You will gain practical experience in a regulated, large-scale technology environment while contributing to services used by customers every day.    A day in the life of IT Risk & Application Security Analyst   • Support application-security and IT-risk assessments for web applications, APIs and digital banking services. • Help identify, document and follow up vulnerabilities, control gaps and remediation actions with development and DevOps teams. • Assist with reviewing security findings from tools and processes such as SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, penetration testing and vulnerability reports. • Contribute to security dashboards, risk registers, evidence collection and management reporting. • Research common threats and weaknesses, including OWASP Top 10 issues, insecure dependencies, authentication risks and CI/CD misconfigurations. • Participate in Agile ceremonies and collaborate with engineers, product owners, security specialists and risk stakeholders. • Help improve practical guidance, checklists and awareness material for secure software development.    How to succeed   We hire for potential. Our biggest expectation is that you stay curious, keep learning and take ownership of your development. In return, we will support you with coaching, meaningful assignments and opportunities to grow into an even more capable version of yourself.    What you bring   • You are currently pursuing, or have recently completed, a bachelor’s or professional training in Cybersecurity, Risk Management or a related field. • Basic understanding of web and API technologies and common software-development practices. • Awareness of application-security concepts and standards, such as OWASP Top 10, secure coding, vulnerability management and risk assessment. • Interested in DevSecOps, CI/CD pipelines, cloud security, threat modelling or security testing. Familiarity with tools such as Git, Azure DevOps, Snyk, SonarQube, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP or similar is an advantage, not a requirement. • Analytical thinking and the ability to translate technical observations into clear risks and actions. • A collaborative mindset, confidence to ask questions and willingness to challenge ideas constructively. • Good written and spoken English. Knowledge of Dutch or French is an asset. ING | Application Security and Risk Analyst Internship    What you will learn  • How application-security and IT-risk controls operate within a major financial institution. • How vulnerabilities are assessed, prioritised, communicated and remediated across multidisciplinary teams. • How secure-software-development practices are integrated into Agile and DevOps delivery. • How to create clear risk insights and practical recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders. • How to work effectively in an international, collaborative and highly regulated environment.    What we offer   • A meaningful internship with hands-on exposure to real application-security and risk challenges. • Guidance from experienced security, risk and engineering professionals. • Access to learning opportunities, internal communities, innovation events and professional-development activities. • An inclusive environment where ideas, curiosity and different perspectives are valued. • The opportunity to build a strong foundation for a career in application security, cyber risk or secure software engineering.

Organizational and administrative skills;   Attention to detail;   Knowledge of Microsoft software and Windows strongly preferred; and   Fluency in Spanish required for Latin America offices.      Fellowship General Qualifications and Required Skills     Bachelor's degree and at least 3+ years of professional experience and/or a graduate degree;  Organizational and administrative skills;   Attention to detail;   Knowledge of Microsoft software and Windows strongly preferred; and   Fluency in Spanish required for Latin America offices.      Critical Qualities     Mature orthodox Christian faith;   Humble and resilient;   Pursues excellence;   Culturally aware and appreciative of difference;   Strong service ethic;   Innovative problem solver;    Ability to build trust and strong partnerships with others;   Courageous in pursuing opportunities and challenges;    Tenacious in achieving goals; and   Professional.     As volunteers, interns and fellows receive a monthly stipend to help defray their expenses related to participating in the internship program. This internship is an ideal opportunity to develop your skills in a real world work environment.  The position develops and performs in-depth review, analysis, and interpretation of all levels of the combined companies' financial activity to identify opportunities to increase revenue, reduce expenses, and provide financial analyses as a management tool.     Discover Your Future with Inmar Intelligence: Where Potential Meets Purpose   For more than 45 years,  Inmar Intelligence  has helped some of the world’s leading brands, retailers, and healthcare organizations solve complex challenges through data, technology, and innovation. Our work has a meaningful impact on everyday life — from helping consumers save money to making healthcare safer and more efficient and helping businesses operate smarter.      Behind that work are people who are curious, collaborative, and motivated to make things better. At Inmar, our  High Challenge, High Support  culture creates an environment where people are encouraged to stretch their thinking, take on meaningful challenges, and grow — with the support and partnership to succeed.     Where Potential Meets Purpose  comes to life through the opportunities our interns have to learn, contribute, and grow. You bring your curiosity, perspective, and what you’ve learned so far. We give you opportunities to put that potential to work on real business challenges, contribute to projects that matter, and learn alongside experienced professionals invested in your growth.      At Inmar, we believe in:     Raising the Bar  in everything we do     Seeking Truth Together  through collaboration and learning      Putting our  Customer First       Your internship is a chance to explore what you’re capable of, build skills through real experience, and begin shaping what comes next.     About This Opportunity   Inmar’s Summer Internship Program offers a dynamic experience designed to give students real-world exposure to a professional environment while contributing meaningfully to company initiatives. Interns split their time between a high-impact cross-functional team project and department-specific responsibilities assigned by their direct manager.      Our  Finance Internship opportunities  provide students with hands-on experience solving real business challenges through financial analysis, data, technology, and process improvement. Depending on the needs of the business, opportunities may be available across areas such as  Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Accounting, Finance Automation, Financial Operations, Accounts Receivable, and other corporate finance functions .      As a Finance intern, you may analyze financial and operational data, support planning and forecasting, improve financial processes, explore automation opportunities, or help teams turn complex information into insights that support better business decisions. You’ll work alongside experienced professionals and cross-functional partners while building both your technical capabilities and your understanding of how Finance helps drive business performance.      Please note: These internship opportunities are expected to be based onsite at our Winston-Salem, NC location and will require in-person attendance during the summer. This posting is intended to build our candidate pipeline for anticipated Summer 2027 Finance internship opportunities. What You May Do   Depending on your internship assignment, you may:      Support  financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and variance analysis  to help teams understand business performance and make informed decisions. What You’ll Gain     Hands-on experience applying finance, accounting, analytics, and problem-solving skills to real business challenges. Experience working with financial and operational data, reporting tools, and evolving technologies.      Opportunities to strengthen your skills in  financial analysis, data storytelling, process improvement, automation, and business partnership .      Mentorship and guidance from experienced Finance professionals.      A better understanding of potential career paths across Finance, Accounting, FP&A, Financial Operations, and Finance technology and automation. jobs.title: Field Operations Intern – SkillBridge
jobs.description: About The Company     Built on a foundation of integrity, respect, and commitment, JPI stands out as one of the most active real estate developers and builders in the nation.  For more than 35 years, JPI has designed and developed communities with best-in-class homes and amenities. JPI is committed to data-driven management and continuous improvement. Its team of experts utilizes data – including unparalleled market research, proven business processes, and proprietary models – to ensure that every decision is strategic, focused, and produces exceptional multifamily communities with the best risk-adjusted returns. More than just great communities, JPI is focused on leaving a lasting impact on the communities where we build and is continually committed to “Building What Matters.”  JPI operates as a subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry, which is recognized as one of the largest home builders in the United States.        Why work for us?        We have a 35-year track record of developing multifamily communities with responsibility, accountability, and integrity.  Our stated purpose is to:      Transform Building      Enhance Communities      Improve Lives           JPI has an ambitious and exciting vision for how we will achieve this, which makes for a positive and dynamic work environment, with many opportunities for personal development and growth.  As well as our highly competitive offering of compensation and benefits, we are committed to:      Transformative careers in a transformative company      Comprehensive training and development      Promotion from within at all levels of the organization      Borderless Careers, based on performance, potential, and personal ambition          Industry Recognition       NMHC - #1 Fastest Growing Developer; #2 Fastest Growing Building; #8 Largest National Developer; # 11 Largest National Builder    Real Page – Most active multifamily developer in DFW for the past 8 years    Dallas Business Journal Best Places to Work – 2023    Dallas Business Journal – Largest DFW Real Estate Developers - #11      JPI offers associates a comprehensive benefits package with competitive salaries and more, including:    Competitive Bonus Program    4 Weeks PTO for All New Associates (Pro-Rated by Hire Date)    11 Holidays and 8 Early Release Days    Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance    401(k) with Company Match (Up to 5% Match)    Health Savings Account    Flexible Spending Accounts (Dependent & Medical Reimbursement)    Paid Parental Leave    Paid Volunteer Time    Tuition Assistance    Phone Reimbursement     Associate Referral Bonuses    About The Job.  JPI has an exciting opportunity for a SkillBridge Intern to join our Recruiting, Training & Development (RTD) and Construction Operations teams through a structured, 180-day transitional training experience designed for Department of Defense SkillBridge participants.  This internship provides progressive exposure to safety, construction operations, field coordination, digital construction tools, and multifamily stage-and-sequence execution through a combination of Academy instruction, Operations Support Center (OSC) rotations, and active jobsite assignments. The program is structured to develop job-ready talent through foundational certifications, mentored field learning, and a capstone project aligned with JPI’s RTD department. Successful participants will build the habits, technical familiarity, and documentation discipline needed to contribute to live project operations from day one after military separation.     ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES       Phase 1: Foundational Orientation, Safety, and OSC Exposure    Complete onboarding and safety readiness activities, including OSHA 30, CPR (as required), and JPI mandatory safety training.  Shadow Operations Support Center (OSC) personnel across designated verticals and complete assigned support tasks that connect to active construction projects.  Learn how centralized support teams contribute to field execution, documentation, communication flow, and issue resolution.  Participate in supervised field orientation activities on an OSC-supported project site (e.g., safety walks, SWPPP observations, EAP awareness, checklist execution, documentation assignments).  Observe and assist with site opening/closing procedures, material receipt, and daily routine support under supervision.  Walk with safety and third-party inspectors to understand compliance expectations and field quality oversight practices.      Phase 2: Academy Training and Technical Development    Complete the Academy curriculum covering JPI culture and mindset, construction technology, construction knowledge, construction operations, and trade operations.  Participate in simulated jobsite scenarios, team-based problem-solving exercises, instructor-led training, and structured site visits.  Complete training in construction technology platforms such as Procore, Bluebeam, OpenSpace, and DroneDeploy.  Successfully complete course assessments measured by accuracy and time-to-complete while meeting participation and professionalism expectations.  Receive and respond to instructor/mentor feedback related to performance, mindset, and growth.      Phase 3: Field Production and Project Oversight Training    Report to the assigned Construction Manager and participate in daily site operations on an active multifamily project.  Support day-to-day GC oversight activities by completing assigned observations, updating status information, and assisting with documentation tied to quality, safety, schedule, and field execution.  Develop working knowledge of multifamily stage-and-sequence responsibilities (horizontal, vertical/rough, exterior/site, finishes, and turnover).  Use JPI construction technology tools in live field conditions to document progress, support accountability, and reinforce project visibility. jobs.description: Who We Are    Johns Manville is a leading manufacturer and marketer of premium-quality insulation and commercial roofing, along with glass fibers and nonwovens for commercial, industrial and residential applications. Our products are used in a wide variety of industries including building products, aerospace, automotive and transportation, filtration, commercial interiors, waterproofing and wind energy.    A proud member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies, we serve customers in more than 80 countries around the globe. We are committed to delivering positive and powerful experiences, because we are successful only when our employees and customers thrive. We are passionate, we care about people, we perform at a superior level, and we protect others and our environments.         Pay Range                                         $41,600.00-$52,600.00 Annual   This is the base salary pay range that an applicant can expect to make upon hire.   Pay within this range will vary based upon relevant experience, skills, and education among other factors.      Johns Manville's Engineered Products business is seeking a highly motivated and analytically minded intern to work directly with the EP Business President and leadership team. This role provides hands-on experience in business analytics, performance management, and AI-enabled decision making within a global manufacturing organization.   We are a hybrid work environment and ask that you are in the office 3 days per week. Our office is in downtown Denver, CO at 717 17 th  St. We do offer free parking or EcoPass.    Key Projects Could Include:    Develop and maintain a daily EP business scorecard  Support development of AI-based decision support tools and help accelerate AI adoption across EP.  Conduct data analysis to support business decisions.  Create dashboards, reports, and insights for executive decision making.  Assist with strategic and operational projects as assigned.     Qualifications:    Bachelors or masters degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Economics, Finance, Data Science, or similar and possesses strong Power BI/Tableau and Excel skills, demonstrates interest in AI applications for manufacturing, and can communicate insights confidently to senior executives.  Local to Denver, CO.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Advanced Excel skills: experience with Power BI, AI tools, or data analytics software is a plus.  Ability to translate data into actionable business recommendations.  Strong communication skills and attention to detail.  Self-starter who can work independently in a fast-paced environment.         #LI-MA1 #LI-HYBIRD #P #D         Please Keep in Mind    If you do not meet 100% of these requirements, we at JM still want to hear from you. So, if you are interested in the role, we encourage you to apply so we can learn how your skills and talents can contribute to our team.     Benefits    Johns Manville (JM) offers a wide range of benefits to employees. Some are subsidized by the company and others are fully employee-paid. Health benefits include a choice of comprehensive medical plans, a dental plan, vision plan, wellness program and critical illness insurance. JM sponsors a 401(k) plan which includes a sizeable company match. JM offers paid vacation and also provides paid sick and parental leave for eligible employees.    Additionally, Johns Manville provides basic life Insurance, short-term and long-term disability coverage, an employee assistance program, and business travel accident coverage. Supplemental life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment insurance are available as well. The company also offers a variety of tax saving accounts; health spending account, traditional flexible spending account, and a dependent care spending account. JM also offers a tuition reimbursement program for undergraduate and certain graduate programs.     Diversity & Inclusion    Johns Manville believes diversity and inclusion in our workplace is critical for the long-term success of our company. This is the right thing to do for our employees, our company and our communities.     Incumbent must be physically able to perform essential job functions. jobs.title: Expression of Interest - Kinrise Internship Program
jobs.description: Kinrise is a growing, privately owned powerhouse in Australian food manufacturing with some of Australia’s most loved and innovative brands. We describe ourselves as a ‘start up with scale’ and have a burning ambition to grow our business. Formed in 2018 the Kinrise portfolio covers Biscuits, Breakfast, Baking, Bakery, and Snackfood categories and has 40+ years making iconic Australian food, with a rich Australian heritage that’s grounded in family origins.      Kickstart your career with real experience in a leading Australian FMCG business.     Kinrise is a proudly Australian owned food manufacturer and home to some of the nation's most loved brands, including  Cobs, Poppin and Greens . We're inviting curious, motivated university students to register their interest in the  Kinrise Internship Program  and gain hands-on experience in a fast-moving food manufacturing business.    This is an  open expression of interest . We'll build a talent pool from the applications we receive and reach out as internship opportunities become available.    Why Kinrise   Our employee promise is  Reach for More : more opportunity to contribute, learn, grow and make a genuine impact. The best learning happens by doing, so you won't sit on the sidelines. You'll join a real team, work on real projects, and see how your contribution connects to our products, our customers and our people.    Depending on your area of study, internships may span Engineering, Manufacturing & Operations, Quality & Food Science, Research & Development, Supply Chain & Logistics, Commercial & Marketing, Finance, Information Technology and People & Culture.    What you'll gain    Hands-on experience in a leading Australian FMCG business  Meaningful project work that makes a genuine contribution  Coaching and support from experienced Kinrise people  Exposure to different teams and career pathways  Opportunities to build your professional network     What we're looking for   We're looking for students who are curious, collaborative and ready to get involved. You don't need all the answers, just energy, a strong work ethic and the willingness to turn what you've learned at university into practical experience.      Before you apply     To help us understand your area of interest and availability, please name your CV using the following format:      First Name and Last Name – Area of Study or Interest – Available Date Range     For example:    John Doe – Supply Chain – 5 January to 20 February 2027     Ready to Reach for More?    Register your interest now.  We'll review every application and contact you should your application progress through the recruitment process.         Why Join Us?       Kinrise is a fast paced, agile business that focuses on your talents and challenges you to perform at your best. An opportunity with us would mean:      An opportunity to work with leading Australian-made brands and products      An exciting role in a growing business with a great history and an ambitious growth agenda      Supportive and collaborative team culture        Kinrise is committed to creating an environment that welcomes all, celebrates our diversity in all its forms and fosters an environment of inclusion. We recognise that our unique differences are what sets us apart and how we succeed as a team. We are an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description: The Olen Corporation and Area Aggregates, one of the largest construction aggregates producers in the Midwest, has been a leader in the industry for over 50 years. With multiple locations serving Central, Northeast, and Northwest Ohio, Olen is dedicated to providing top-quality aggregate products, including natural sand, gravel, and limestone, to a diverse range of customers. As an ODOT 1069 prequalified aggregates supplier, Olen sets the standard for quality and service in the industry. Producing over 8 million tons of construction materials each year, Olen is a top thirty-five national producer of quality construction aggregates. Since 1986, Olen has partnered with Kokosing to be one of their top suppliers of construction materials. Committed to excellence, Olen is focused on delivering exceptional customer service while being responsible stewards of the environment and respectful neighbors in the communities we serve.      Job Description:     About Olen Corporation    Olen Corporation, a division of Kokosing, is one of Ohio's leading aggregate producers, supplying high-quality construction materials that support critical infrastructure and development projects throughout the state. Operating multiple limestone quarry and aggregate facilities, Olen produces more than  8 million tons of aggregate annually , serving a diverse range of customers and projects.   Our co-op program offers students a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in quarry and mining operations while working alongside industry professionals dedicated to safety, innovation, and operational excellence. Assist with hazard identification and corrective action processes.  Learn environmental compliance and sustainable mining practices.    Quality Control & Materials Testing    Assist with aggregate sampling, testing, and quality assurance procedures.  Learn industry specifications and standards for construction materials.  Support quality control initiatives to ensure customer and project requirements are met.  Gain experience with laboratory testing equipment and reporting. Learn plant automation systems and production monitoring technology.  Assist with project planning and capital improvement activities.    Maintenance & Equipment Reliability    Gain hands-on experience with preventive and corrective maintenance activities.  Assist in troubleshooting mechanical breakdowns and operational challenges. Equipment Operation & Field Experience    Observe and gain exposure to heavy equipment operation.  Learn the role and capabilities of various mining and construction equipment. Learn how construction materials are integrated into major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Ohio.  Develop an understanding of production forecasting, inventory management, and market demand. Ability to work safely in a quarry and industrial environment.  Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.  Willingness to work outdoors and in varying weather conditions.     Preferred    Prior internship, co-op, or construction experience.  Familiarity with engineering principles, equipment systems, or industrial operations.  Interest in pursuing a career in the mining, aggregates, construction materials, or heavy civil construction industries.     What You Will Gain    Through this co-op experience, students will:   Develop a comprehensive understanding of aggregate production and mining operations.  Gain hands-on field experience in one of Ohio's largest aggregate operations.  Work alongside experienced managers, engineers, mechanics, and operators.  Learn how quality construction materials support major infrastructure and building projects.  Build technical, operational, and leadership skills applicable to careers in engineering, construction, mining, and operations management. jobs.title: Support Operations & Equipment Group Co-op Summer 2027
jobs.description: Kokosing (www.kokosing.biz) is one of America's 50 largest General Contractors and services a broad spectrum of clients in both the private and public business sectors. Kokosing's services include heavy civil/industrial construction such as highways, bridges, underground utilities, water/wastewater facilities, and marine construction. For over 75 years, Kokosing has successfully attracted the most qualified technical personnel in the construction industry by offering visible challenges, superior quality, and attractive rewards. With over $2.8 billion in annual sales and a commitment to its workforce, Kokosing is the winning team.      Job Description:    The  Co-op Program at Kokosing  is designed to provide you with practical industry experience, meaningful responsibilities, mentorship from experienced professionals, and opportunities to connect with senior leaders, team members, and fellow co-ops.   As a Support Operations Co-op, you will gain hands-on experience supporting the people, equipment, materials, and processes that keep construction projects running safely and efficiently. Working alongside mechanics, equipment managers, shop personnel, engineers, and operations teams, you'll contribute to real-world projects involving heavy equipment maintenance, fleet operations, material management, fabrication, logistics, and technical support functions.   We are seeking students interested in co-op opportunities during the Spring, Summer, or Fall semesters across our operating regions. Support preventative maintenance programs that help maximize equipment reliability and performance.  Learn equipment diagnostics, troubleshooting, and repair processes under the guidance of experienced mechanics and technicians.  Assist with tracking equipment utilization, maintenance records, warranties, and service schedules.  Support warehouse, inventory, and material management processes.  Assist with ordering, receiving, organizing, and tracking parts, tools, and construction materials. Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on equipment performance, productivity, and operational efficiency. jobs.title: Intern, Accounting
jobs.description: Thank you for your interest in the BWL. We think you'll find it a rewarding and nurturing place to grow your career.   Starting Salary Range: $23.00 - $23.00      Job Description   The Lansing Board of Water & Light (BWL) has an opening for an  Accounting Intern  in our General Accounting Department, located in Lansing, MI.   Position Summary:    Job Type: Full-Time Summer Internship  Dates: May 17, 2027 - August 13, 2027  Pay Rate: $23.00 per hour.   The Accounting Intern will learn various analytics and will support accounting enhancement projects.  They will support the company’s business units by providing the tools and knowledge needed for consistent and effective decision making. The Accounting Interns will learn from, and be supervised by, a mentor and those within the General Accounting Department.     Essential Functions:    Assist with current projects to include, but not limited to:  Capital project creation, maintenance, and closure.  Capital asset review and in-service activity.  Navigate SAP to run reports, record accounting transactions, and research ledger detail history.  Assigned accounting projects, which may include but are not limited to account reconciliations, identifying and collecting support for audit requests, and miscellaneous research    Utilizes standard office software (i.e., spreadsheet, word-processing, database) and SAP.  Required to follow BWL Safety Manual and wear personal protective equipment for all field location visits.  Attends training and safety awareness and/or skills improvement as required by the BWL or government agency such as MIOSHA.  Expected to comply with all BWL policies and work rules.  Predictable and reliable attendance.  Other duties as assigned by supervisor.      Job Specifications:    Currently enrolled in an accredited educational institution with a focus on Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration, or a related field with junior or senior status during the summer of 2027.  Must be enrolled in fall classes 2027.  Minimum GPA of 3.0  A cover letter is requested with your submission, please.     Interviews will begin mid-November.      Physical Requirements / Working Conditions:     The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.    Employees are required to follow the BWL Safety Manual and wear required personal protective equipment, adhere to BWL safety rules and regulations, attend all training for safety awareness or skills improvement as required by supervisors, BWL, or governmental agency such as MIOSHA. Normal office and occasional field work.  Field conditions may include heat, cold, dust, and/or noise.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.  The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, and ability to adjust focus, especially due to concentration on a computer screen and small numbers.    Must successfully complete a background check, a substance screening and a physical (if applicable).       The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position.  They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and skills that may be required of the employee.  Management reserves the right to add, remove, or otherwise alter these duties, responsibilities, and skills at any time.      About BWL:  The Board of Water & Light serves Lansing, Michigan, and surrounding areas with electricity, water, and steam. Lansing's city charter vests the BWL with full and exclusive management of water, steam, and electric services for or the city. The American Public Power Association has honored the Lansing Board of Water & Light as one of the country's best publicly-owned utilities.    The Location:  Lansing lies at the heart of the Great Lakes State and offers all the beauty and splendor of the four seasons. A haven for swimming, boating, fishing, snowmobiling, golf, and hunting, mid-Michigan is also just a couple hours from premier skiing and one of the most beautiful freshwater lakeshores in the world on our Lake Michigan Coast. Lansing itself is only minutes and miles away from two of the nation’s premier universities, Michigan State University and the University of Michigan, and boasts miles of walking, running, biking trails, Potter Park Zoo, professional sports, the arts, and fine dining.       THE BOARD OF WATER & LIGHT IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

jobs.title: Internship: Quantitative Research Analyst
jobs.description: Bridging the gap between academia and industry.  Scientific Beta is a wholly owned subsidiary of    STOXX Ltd   . Following its acquisition by STOXX on 8 July 2026, the company continues to build on the strong foundations established throughout its history, maintaining the principles of independent, empirical-based academic research that has defined Scientific Beta since its creation.    Scientific Beta was established in 2012 by the EDHEC-Risk Institute, one of the top academic institutions in the field of fundamental and applied research for the investment industry. We pioneer the latest advances in smart factor and ESG/Climate index design and implementation, with a mission to encourage adoption by industry peers. Our academic heritage means we have a relentless focus on scientific rigour and precision, and we apply this to all aspects of our service provision to clients. Our smart factor and ESG/Climate solutions are proven scientifically, with full transparency of both our methods and the associated risks.      As part of its index development activity, Scientific Beta is recruiting  two   interns for quantitative research analysis . The position is based in Nice, France.      Internship: Quantitative Research Analyst - Two vacancies in Nice, France – Full-time    The internship is for a period of six months, starting in January 2027.  The interns will conduct quantitative research on systematic equity investment strategies. They will analyse the performance of these strategies over time and across market conditions, assess implementation issues and transaction costs, and examine and document the portfolio construction process. They will interpret and communicate their findings, including through reports and presentation materials.  Candidates should have strong programming skills (Python preferred), a solid command of financial theory and applied econometrics, and a demonstrated interest in empirical work with financial data.   If you wish to apply for this position, please provide a cover letter, your CV, and a transcript of grades from your MSc courses.   #LI-TG1 #STOXX #INTERNSHIP    What You Can Expect from Us   Our people are the moving force behind our work. We are committed to building a culture that values diverse skills, perspectives, and experiences. If you have the skills, passion, and drive to help us bring clarity and transparency to capital markets, we want to work with you.     Together, we can grow your career in an environment that fuels creativity, drives innovation, and has real impact.    About ISS STOXX   ISS STOXX delivers world-class research, data, and technology solutions that empower capital market participants to pursue their visions with confidence. Our expertise spans indices, corporate governance, sustainability, cyber risk, and fund intelligence, giving clients the tools they need to uncover opportunities, manage risks, and navigate evolving regulations. We are made up of 4,000 professionals operating across 20 countries and serving approximately 5,000 clients, including many of the world’s leading institutional investors. Our scale and reach give us deep market knowledge, while our innovative methodologies allow us to offer our clients tailored insights that drive impact and success.       ISS STOXX Indices , including the renowned STOXX and DAX families, sets the standard for rules-based, transparent, and liquid benchmarks and indices. Our ready-made products and customized solutions are used by sophisticated institutional investors, ETF issuers, and providers of derivatives and structured products.        Visit our website:     https://www.iss-stoxx.com/           Learn more:    https://stoxx.com/      View additional open roles:     https://www.iss-stoxx.com/about/careers/           ISS STOXX is committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity and inclusion. It is our policy to prohibit discrimination or harassment against any applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, creed, religion, sex, age, height, weight, citizenship status, national origin, social origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression, pregnancy status, marital status, familial status, mental or physical disability, veteran status, military service or status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law (referred to as “protected status”).  All activities including, but not limited to, recruiting and hiring, recruitment advertising, promotions, performance appraisals, training, job assignments, compensation, demotions, transfers, terminations (including layoffs), benefits, and other terms, conditions, and privileges of employment, are and will be administered on a non-discriminatory basis, consistent with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.

jobs.title: Pricing AI & Data Analytics Intern
jobs.description: Turn data into insights and help shape the future of pricing!     Would you like to explore how AI can make complex pricing information more accessible and valuable? Join our Pricing team and help us develop a generative AI assistant that enables colleagues to get fast, reliable answers to their pricing questions.     What makes this internship unique is that it is about more than solving a technical problem. Besides understanding how large language models (LLMs) work, you will dive into the business to discover what information colleagues really need to make better pricing decisions. This combination of technology and business understanding gives you a tangible project with a direct impact on the organisation.      Your role     As a Pricing AI & Data Analytics Intern, you will work closely with the Pricing team to develop a generative AI assistant that can answer questions related to pricing. You will define the right context – the relevant data, definitions and business logic – and let an LLM process that context so it can provide accurate answers. To do this well, you will need to understand both how LLMs work and what information the business needs, transforming complex pricing data into accessible and actionable insights.     Your specific tasks include:     Contribute to the design and development of a generative AI assistant that can understand and respond to pricing-related questions.      Engage with stakeholders across the business to understand which pricing questions they have and what information they need to answer them.      Extract, process and analyse large datasets from different sources and structure them into the right context for the LLM, making relevant pricing information accessible and usable.      Explore and apply AI tools and technologies, such as Microsoft Copilot and other relevant solutions, to develop and improve the assistant's capabilities.      Use tools to analyse data, identify patterns and support the development of the solution.      Collaborate with Pricing and Data Science colleagues to translate business needs into technical solutions and continuously improve the assistant.       Your team     You will be part of the Pricing team and report directly to the Head of Pricing. You will work closely with the other members of the team. In addition, you will collaborate with the Data Science team and Pricing Managers, combining pricing expertise with technical and analytical capabilities to develop an effective AI solution.      Who are you?     You are curious, analytical and enthusiastic about exploring how data and AI can solve real business challenges. You enjoy working with complex datasets, experimenting with new technologies and are just as interested in understanding the business as in understanding the technology. You like translating technical possibilities into practical solutions.     For this role, we have a few key requirements:     You are currently pursuing a Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Business Analytics, Statistics or a related field.      You have a strong understanding of data analysis and experience working with large datasets. You are comfortable querying, processing and interpreting data.      You have experience with programming and data tools such as Python, R, SQL and/or Google BigQuery. Experience with Tableau or other data visualisation tools is a plus.      You have a genuine interest in artificial intelligence and generative AI assistants. Familiarity with Microsoft Copilot, large language models (LLMs) or similar technologies is an advantage.      You have a strong analytical and problem-solving mindset, are able to break down complex questions and enjoy translating business needs into practical technical solutions.             Do you want to join us?         In case you feel challenged by the above role description and requirements, we are interested in meeting you! Please use the application button and send your CV and cover letter.       If you do not fully meet all requirements for this role, and you think you would be a good match for us, please apply and convince us.       Do you have a question about this role? Please do not hesitate to contact Eirini Dragoumanou, Talent Acquisition Specialist, eirini.dragoumanou@kramp.com         About us         Thanks to our ambitions we are active throughout Europe: a leading position in the agricultural market for parts. We heavily invest in E-Business and innovations. Our aim is to make it easy for our customers to run their business. Working at Kramp means working with over 3500 international colleagues. The people at Kramp are enthusiastic, professional and involved. We speak our customers’ language, understand their challenges and earn their trust to exceed their expectations. Our promise “It’s that easy” is embedded in our culture and DNA.              Working at Kramp means:        … you belong here! ​Being part of our open business community​        … your work makes a difference!​ Have an impact on what matters        … you will develop and realize​! Learn and realize your potential         More about Kramp:       https://www.careeratkramp.com/nl-nl               #LI-ED1   Varsseveld - Breukelaarweg     Location:     Utrecht

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Commercial Bank Internship - Cleveland (Credit)
jobs.description:
Location:  127 Public Square, Cleveland Ohio       If you are interested in more than one KeyBank Internship opportunity, please consider applying for your top 3 internship roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts and obtaining the best candidate experience.      The Commercial Bank internship will provide an experience to understand the Commercial Banking landscape and how the various line of business functions collaborate to provide clients/prospects with the insights and solutions they need to operate their business more effectively.      Program Duration: MAY 26, 2027 – AUGUST 6, 2027        What does our Internship Program offer?    Key’s Enterprise Internship is a 10.5-week program that provides meaningful work that matters, offers feedback and coaching, and creates engaging events and conversations that will spark excitement and interest in bringing one’s full-time career to Key.  Interns are involved in a host of line of business specific projects that directly impact and benefit Key’s business and strategic pillars. The program includes networking with Key teammates across all levels of the organization, a series of Learning Labs where internal and external speakers provide insight on Key’s competitive landscape, financial wellness, and professional development best practices, and an assigned mentor who shares knowledge, experience, and advice.      Commercial Banking    Commercial at Key offers a comprehensive suite of financial solutions tailored to support the growth, liquidity, and risk management needs of middle market and institutional clients. What differentiates us from competitors is our ability to seamlessly deliver comprehensive industry expertise, unique insight and capital markets solutions. This includes services such as lending, commercial payments (treasury), and advisory support. As a core component of Key’s strategic priorities, the Commercial Bank plays a vital role in driving client success and contributing to the company’s overall performance.      About the Internship     As an intern, you will gain valuable experience by contributing to a variety of projects and collaborating closely with seasoned professionals. This role offers a focus on credit/lending (relationship management) specifically within the Cleveland Market. You will engage directly with senior-level bankers and Commercial Analysts, providing hands-on exposure to the Commercial Lending business. You will receive exposure to various segments within the Commercial Bank, as well.      Job Responsibilities    Learn to analyze commercial loan requests via loan requests including but not limited to reviewing financial statement spreads; calculation of key financial ratios; analysis of the borrowers’ business and financial integrity  Work closely with designated teams to ensure accuracy of credit system data.  Work with clients to ensure timely collection of financial statements needed to monitor performance  Work with support partners to perform system maintenance to ensure proper portfolio assignments and with Relationship Managers to ensure accurate pipeline activities within Salesforce  Complete a Capstone Project leveraging learnings from the Internship to include credit, business analytics, and client facing deliverables / pitches  Perform other duties as necessary to support the goals and objectives of the relationship management teams      Qualifications    Must have completed at least two years toward a four-year, undergraduate degree program with coursework in finance, accounting, economics and/or data science (preferred) with an anticipated graduation in or before May of 2028    Outstanding academic achievement (minimum undergraduate 3.3 GPA)  Demonstrated leadership and teamwork from past work experience and/or extracurricular activities  Strong quantitative and critical thinking abilities  Highly motivated with a strong work ethic  Outstanding interpersonal, communication and presentation skills  Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint  Professional conduct      Compensation and Benefits   This position is eligible to earn an hourly rate of $23 per hour. Compensation also includes a $2,000 Summer Internship Sign-on Bonus.     KeyBank’s Internship and Analyst positions are not eligible for employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B visa). This includes, for example, situations where a candidate may have temporary work authorization while enrolled in school or upon graduation (e.g., CPT, OPT) but would need H-1B visa sponsorship within a few years of employment in order to maintain employment eligibility.     COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS  This position is compensated at a fixed rate of $23 hourly and is eligible to receive a $2,000 sign-on bonus.    Please click    here    for a list of benefits for which this position is eligible.    Key has implemented an approach to employee workspaces which prioritizes in-office presence, while providing flexible options in circumstances where roles can be performed effectively in a mobile environment. jobs.title: Director, NIL Revenue & Activation - Ohio State University
jobs.description: The Director, NIL Revenue & Activation will serve as Buckeye Sports Properties strategic lead for all Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) initiatives. This individual will be responsible for aligning NIL strategy with institutional values and NCAA/conference guidelines, driving revenue through NIL-related opportunities, and ensuring flawless execution of athlete engagements. This role bridges key internal and external relationships, including athletics administration, coaches, compliance, creative services, brand partners, and donors.   The ideal candidate will be an experienced leader with a strong background in sports marketing, athlete relations, sponsorship sales, and overall revenue generation. They must be able to operate autonomously in a fast-paced environment, balancing day-to-day activation with long-term strategic planning.      Key Responsibilities:     NIL Strategy & Leadership    Drive NIL Dealmaking Revenue strategy, support all NIL sales efforts with the Sports Properties Team, manage and lead dedicated NIL Sports Properties staff (sales and fulfillment)     Design and implement a sustainable NIL infrastructure aligned with university values, athletic priorities, and national regulations.    Partner with athletics leadership and internal units (e.g., development, MMR, compliance) to optimize NIL strategy and athlete opportunities.    Lead evaluations of NIL revenue potential, staffing needs, and organizational processes for continued growth.    Provide strategic input on potential revenue-sharing models, athlete incentives, and policies that support a competitive NIL ecosystem.     NIL Operations & Administration    Oversee daily NIL operations, including fulfillment, local deal flow, athlete education, and stakeholder coordination.  Serve as the primary liaison between student-athletes, brand partners, and the athletics department.  Ensure accurate dissemination of deal metrics and uphold internal and external compliance standards.     Athlete Relations & Contracting    Act as point of contact for athletes on NIL opportunity awareness, fulfillment, and support.  Collaborate with legal and compliance on contract reviews and risk mitigation, including House settlement terms.  Support recruiting and retention efforts by developing custom NIL pitch materials and activation examples for coaches.     Business Development & Partner Collaboration    Partner with the MMR sales team to align NIL initiatives with existing and new sponsorship revenue opportunities.  Lead and participate in brand partner conversations, including non-sponsor NIL deals and donor engagement.  Oversee packaging, pricing strategies, proposal development, and contract finalization.  Identify and promote NIL revenue opportunities that extend beyond existing sponsorship structures or traditional athletics budgets.     Oversight of Events, Operations & Creative    Provide leadership oversight (but not direct execution) of NIL-related events, content creation, social media strategy, and facility management.  Support the execution of NIL marketing campaigns and events in collaboration with content and operations staff.  Monitor success metrics and athlete brand development using social and performance data.     Minimum Qualifications:    Bachelor’s degree preferred  Minimum 8 years of relevant experience including but not limited to NIL, sponsorship, athlete marketing, or sports business.  Strong understanding of NCAA/compliance regulations, NIL trends, and the collegiate athletics landscape.  Proven experience leading teams, developing strategy, and driving revenue growth.  Excellent communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.  Comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-evolving NIL environment.  Experience developing or supporting content strategies for social media, with a clear sense of what drives engagement across different platforms.  Familiarity with creative production elements such as graphic design, motion graphics, photography, and social storytelling.  Understanding digital and social media best practices within NIL and influencer marketing. PURPOSE:  The Associate Director of Student Accounting and Bursar Operations position oversees the daily operations of Student Accounting and Bursar Operations, ensuring accurate student account management, cashiering, tuition and fee assessment, student refunds, and exceptional customer service.        RESPONSIBILITIES:   ·         Manage all student financial appeal processes and adjust This role combines day-to-day exposure to the real estate investment sales business with structured education, training, and mentorship, including workshops and networking opportunities. Interns work in-office as part of a brokerage team.
   Background   Marcus & Millichap is the industry’s largest firm specializing in real estate investment sales and financing, as well as a leading source of research and advisory services. The Investment Brokerage Internship is designed to provide current college students with meaningful exposure to the commercial real estate industry and a foundation for pursuing a career in investment sales.   The anticipated compensation is $20 - $25/hr. The final compensation offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to the type of experience within the industry, education, etc. Marcus & Millichap is a multi-state employer, and this hourly range may not reflect positions that work in other states.    Benefits:  EAP (Employee Assistance Program) and Paid Time Off.    During the course of the 8-week program, Investment Brokerage Interns will:    Garner real-life commercial real estate experience through in-office participation in team projects, sales meetings and the creation of contracts, Broker Opinion of Values (BOVs), and Offering Memorandums (OMs).  Gain access to outstanding training and education, including workshops and exclusive Marcus & Millichap University classes covering financing, business development, underwriting, and more.  Make career-changing connections through your Marcus & Millichap mentor and networking opportunities with senior agents and management.  Attend informative conversations with top Marcus & Millichap agents and learn how to forge profitable relationships, develop winning proposals, build key selling skills and more.  Earn a competitive salary while confirming your interest in the CRE profession and bolstering your industry skill set.     Application Requirements:    Rising college juniors or seniors  Enrolled at an accredited university  Pursuing a real estate minor or major or participating in a real estate club or boot camp     No Visa sponsorship is available at this time    Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply early, as opportunities may fill before the deadline.   Marcus & Millichap is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.

This role combines day-to-day exposure to the real estate investment sales business with structured education, training, and mentorship, including workshops and networking opportunities. Interns work in-office as part of a brokerage team.
   Background   Marcus & Millichap is the industry’s largest firm specializing in real estate investment sales and financing, as well as a leading source of research and advisory services. The Investment Brokerage Internship is designed to provide current college students with meaningful exposure to the commercial real estate industry and a foundation for pursuing a career in investment sales.   The anticipated compensation is $20 - $25/hr. The final compensation offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to the type of experience within the industry, education, etc. Marcus & Millichap is a multi-state employer, and this hourly range may not reflect positions that work in other states.    Benefits:  EAP (Employee Assistance Program) and Paid Time Off.    During the course of the 8-week program, Investment Brokerage Interns will:    Garner real-life commercial real estate experience through in-office participation in team projects, sales meetings and the creation of contracts, Broker Opinion of Values (BOVs), and Offering Memorandums (OMs).  Gain access to outstanding training and education, including workshops and exclusive Marcus & Millichap University classes covering financing, business development, underwriting, and more.  Make career-changing connections through your Marcus & Millichap mentor and networking opportunities with senior agents and management.  Attend informative conversations with top Marcus & Millichap agents and learn how to forge profitable relationships, develop winning proposals, build key selling skills and more.  Earn a competitive salary while confirming your interest in the CRE profession and bolstering your industry skill set.     Application Requirements:    Rising college juniors or seniors  Enrolled at an accredited university  Pursuing a real estate minor or major or participating in a real estate club or boot camp     No Visa sponsorship is available at this time    Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply early, as opportunities may fill before the deadline.   Marcus & Millichap is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.

Participate fully in the activities and programs of SMSU’s Business Innovation & Strategy Department  Fulfill the expectations of a full-time probationary faculty member at SMSU in accordance with SMSU’s Assessment and Strategic Plan and its mission, vision, and values. Minimum Qualifications    Ph.D. or DBA with an emphasis in accounting from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants holding a Master's degree in Accounting and an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license issued by a state board of accountancy will also be considered.  Experience teaching and/or developing undergraduate accounting courses.  Evidence of teaching experience in classroom, online, and/or hybrid instructional formats.  Evidence of written communication skills through application materials and professional, academic, or scholarly work    Preferred Qualification     Teaching experience in accounting courses at the undergraduate level.  Professional work experience in accounting outside of academia.  Demonstrate the ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, and business/community groups, including but not limited to participating in department accreditation events, student club advising, etc.  Evidence of teaching performance through student evaluations, peer evaluations, teaching awards, or other documented measures.  Evidence of current scholarly activity.  Experience advising, mentoring, coaching, or supporting students through student organizations, internships, research activities, or academic advising. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to teach and work with people from diverse backgrounds.  Professional certifications such as CPA, CMA, CIA, CFE, CGMA, or related credentials.       Priority will be given to those who apply by 10/1/2026.        Required documents to submit for consideration:  Cover Letter, Resume/CV, Transcript(s), Teaching Philosophy, and Diversity Statement.       Other Considerations:  The successful candidate must be authorized to work in the United States by the first day of employment. The University will not consider H-1B sponsorship. Employment or Visa sponsorship, other than H-1B status, must be pre-approved by the University prior to offer acceptance. The 216-acre campus encompasses 24 modern, interconnected, and accessible buildings. Marshall (pop. 13,000) is the hub of a rich agricultural area and offers a variety of cultural, recreational and educational opportunities.
