jobs.title: Liquidnet Fixed Income Sales & Trading Internship
jobs.description: About TP ICAP Group & Liquidnet   TP ICAP Group is the world’s largest interdealer broker, connecting buyers and sellers across global financial, energy, and commodities markets. The Group operates through several divisions, including Global Broking, Agency Execution, and Data & Analytics.     Liquidnet sits within TP ICAP’s Agency Execution division. Acquired by the Group in 2021, Liquidnet is a next‑generation agency execution specialist. Its trading and liquidity network intelligently and securely connects the world’s investors with the world’s investments, helping institutional clients drive alpha through smarter execution.     Founded in 1999, Liquidnet was built on the belief that trading could be more efficient, collaborative, and confident. Today, as part of TP ICAP Group, it remains a thriving ecosystem that empowers the buy side in ways never before imagined.           Program Overview     Our Fixed Income Summer Internship offers a dynamic immersion into the front office trading environment at Liquidnet. Interns gain hands‑on exposure to the processes, relationships, and market activity that drive our fixed income execution business.           You’ll be embedded directly within the Fixed Income Sales & Trading team, working alongside professionals who connect institutional clients to liquidity across bonds and credit products. This structure provides both real‑time market learning and opportunities to collaborate across the broader organization.            Program dates: Tuesday, June 1– Friday, August 6, 2027             Your Experience     As our Fixed Income Sales & Trading intern, your summer will be shaped by real exposure to the trading floor. You’ll spend your days shadowing coverage teams, supporting client interactions, and monitoring fixed income market activity.         Your day‑to‑day will include:     Shadowing Fixed Income coverage during live trading sessions.    Monitoring real‑time activity in the Liquidnet system to understand bond and credit flows.    Assisting with client requests and onboarding in collaboration with product support and legal teams.    Supporting the Sales team with client performance analysis and reporting.    Learning how Transaction Cost Analysis (TCA) informs fixed income execution strategies.    Contributing to desk‑specific projects that improve client engagement and trading efficiency.    Conducting ad hoc analyses to investigate trading or operational issues.          You’ll gain perspective on how Fixed Income professionals build relationships, manage client flow, and deliver execution outcomes in fast‑moving credit markets.            Culture, Programming & Mentorship     We aim to create a summer experience that’s both professionally enriching and genuinely fun. Beyond your team, interns participate in structured programming designed to broaden your skills and network, including:          Learning & Development Workshops    Volunteer and Community Engagement Events    Social and Networking Activities          Each intern is matched with a dedicated mentor to support their development throughout the program. Mentors provide career advice, help navigate the firm, and serve as sounding boards for questions and ideas.            Eligibility Criteria     To be considered, candidates must:     Be currently enrolled in an undergraduate program and pursuing a bachelor’s degree.    Have an anticipated graduation date between December 2026 and June 2027.    Be authorized to work in the United States (we do not offer visa sponsorship).    Relocate at own cost if applicable; Liquidnet does not provide relocation or housing assistance.             Ideal Candidates     We’re looking for students who are:     Passionate about fixed income markets and client interaction.    Strong communicators who can build relationships and collaborate effectively.    Curious learners with analytical thinking and problem‑solving skills.    Adaptable and composed in fast‑changing, high‑pressure environments.    Organized and detail‑oriented, able to manage multiple tasks with precision.    Comfortable with Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel); familiarity with Bloomberg or market data tools is a plus.             Salary     ·         $34.00 / hour         If you’re ready to explore the fast‑paced world of Fixed Income Sales & Trading while building your professional network, we encourage you to apply now!        #LNET #LI-INT #LI-Onsite       About TP ICAP Group   The TP ICAP Group is a world-leading provider of financial markets infrastructure and data. Our purpose is to provide clients with access to global financial and commodities markets, improving price discovery, liquidity, and distribution of data, through responsible and innovative solutions. Through our people and technology, we connect clients to superior liquidity and data solutions. The Group is home to a stable of premium brands. Collectively, TP ICAP is the largest interdealer broker in the world by revenue, a leading Energy & Commodities broker, the world’s leading provider of OTC data, and an award winning all-to-all trading platform. Founded in London in 1866, the Group operates from more than 60 offices in 28 countries. We work as one to achieve our vision of being the world’s most trusted, innovative, liquidity and data solutions specialist.      Not The Perfect Fit?   If you’re concerned about not meeting every requirement, we want to reassure you: TP ICAP is deeply committed to inclusivity and building a work environment where everyone can thrive, no matter their background. If you’re excited about this role but feel your experience doesn’t check every box, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this position or another within our organisation. Our Talent Acquisition team is here to help you discover how your unique talents could make a meaningful impact. Don’t hesitate to take the leap and explore new possibilities with us—your potential is what matters most.

Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving abilities, including the ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information.  Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively.  Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.                                        Job Category                                     Actuarial    Compensation Overview   The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.      Salary Range  $28.00 - $33.00                                       Target Openings                                     32                                                                                                               What Is the Opportunity?                                                                                                             Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future.  The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role.      Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis beginning in early-mid September. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.      The goal of the Actuarial Leadership Development Program (ALDP) internship is to attract and develop self-motivated individuals who are highly skilled and passionate about a career in actuarial while providing a foundation for future success within the organization. As an ALDP intern, you will be exposed to a challenging actuarial professional work experience with planned activities giving you insight into business and the many actuarial career options at Travelers. With many company-wide events such as Intern Symposium and community outreach events, you will have the opportunity to interact and network with many levels of leadership and management. You may have an opportunity to work together with fellow interns to develop and present solutions to relevant business and actuarial topics.       Housing: The Internship program is based in Hartford, CT and St. Paul, MN. Positions are available in our business units and corporate departments. Subsidized apartments are available for students who live beyond a commutable distance from Hartford, CT or St. Paul, MN. Positions are available early June through the end of the summer.  What Will You Do?    The ALDP internship has a wide variety of actuarial assignments across numerous Business Lines in areas such as: Pricing and Ratemaking, Reserving, Claim, Risk Analysis, Product Management, Corporate/Enterprise, and Data Science.  The ALDP Summer Internship Program provides qualified students an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand business experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn about the many actuarial and analytic positions available in the insurance industry. Interns are provided exposure to all levels of management and have the chance to collaborate and network with other development programs during business workshops, work assignments, and social events. You will learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.  ALDP interns are viewed as a primary source of future candidates for entry level actuarial and analytic careers within the company. They receive challenging work assignments that add value and impact the business.  Perform other duties as assigned.    What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?    Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater preferred.  Completion of one or more actuarial exams.  Suggested degree majors are Actuarial Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Finance, Computer Science or a related field.  Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel.      What is a Must Have?    Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree.       Employment Practices     Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.       We are committed to providing accommodation to persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation during the recruitment or interview process we will work with you to accommodate your needs.      If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an     email     so we may assist you.      Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.      To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit      http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/     .

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.    Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP).     Housing assistance is not provided.  What Will You Do?    Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:  Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.  Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.  Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.  Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.  Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.  Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.  Perform other duties as assigned.     What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?    Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. 
 Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance. 
 Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.      What is a Must Have?    Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor’s degree.       Employment Practices     Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. At Travelers, our vision is to advance our ability to fuel analytic-driven business decisions by accelerating cross-enterprise collaboration and capabilities.    The Business Insights & Analytics Leadership Development Program (BI&ALDP) internship is built for analytically driven students who are serious about launching a career in data and analytics. This is not a passive, observational internship — you will do real work, solve real business problems, and be evaluated like a professional from day one.      Over 10 weeks, you and your cohort of peers will be embedded in Travelers' data and analytics community, gaining hands-on experience in one or more of our core analytics disciplines while building the technical and professional skills that define a successful career.       Technical training is delivered to you by current full-time BI&ALDP participants — those who were recently in your position — giving you an authentic, peer-informed perspective on what it takes to grow here.      Housing: The internship program is based in Hartford, CT and St. Paul, MN. Positions are available in our business units and corporate departments. Subsidized apartments are available for students who live beyond a commutable distance from Hartford, CT or St. Paul, MN.      Positions are available from June through early August.  What Will You Do?    Real project work aligned to active business needs across Travelers' analytics functions.  Technical training taught by full-time BI&ALDP participants.  Formal performance reviews that give you honest, structured feedback on your growth.  Leadership exposure through company-wide events including the Intern Symposium and community outreach initiatives, where you will interact with leaders and a cohort across the enterprise.  A collaborative capstone presentation where you and your fellow interns develop and present solutions to relevant business and analytics challenges.  Leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.  At the close of the internship, high performing interns are eligible to interview for a full-time offer to join the BI&ALDP — making these 10 weeks one of the most important career opportunities of your academic journey.  Perform other duties as assigned.    What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?    Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater preferred.  Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a STEM related discipline (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Math).  Data warehouse and ETL understanding with Python, SQL, and/or Snowflake.  Knowledge of data lakes and/or experience with Databricks.  Exposure to dashboarding, scorecards or other descriptive reporting tools.  Knowledge of multidimensional data and open-source cloud-enabled analytical programming languages.  Familiarity with agile concepts & workflows.      What is a Must Have?    Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree. jobs.title: Operations Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. – Publicly Traded US Company, NASDAQ (TTMI) – Top-5 Global Printed Circuit Board Manufacturer     About TTM      TTM Technologies, Inc. is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency (“RF”) components, RF microwave/microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (“PCB”s). TTM stands for time-to-market, representing how TTM's time-critical, one-stop design, engineering and manufacturing services enable customers to reduce the time required to develop new products and bring them to market  .    Additional information can be found at www.ttm.com       TTM offers summer internships to qualified Management students who are looking to gain professional experience in their field of study. Internships are designed to help build your professional credentials by providing meaningful, practical, on-the-job training and experiences, while also igniting your imagination.     Opportunities exist throughout our company and are available to students who are motivated to learn and grow. You will get a chance to contribute your best ideas and work in an environment that inspires innovative results. Students in our internship program provide tremendous value to our organization through increased productivity, introduction of innovative, fresh ideas and talent, and often become reliable and skilled permanent employees.     The TTM Internship Program is geared toward juniors who are going into their senior year of college. It is a stimulating and rewarding experience, helping the student make the transition from school to work and career while motivating the student for a potential manufacturing, engineering & technology future. Participating in one of our internships is also invaluable in establishing a network within the company.     This position is located at our 234 Cashman Drive location.      Program Outline:      Each internship project selection will include 1 major and 1-2 minor projects, all deliverable within the summer period of 12-14 weeks.    Present multiple project updates to the local leadership team    The Program will include some additional training/teambuilding activities.      Essential Knowledge and Skills:      The student must be enrolled in an accredited college or university Management undergraduate program, and be a junior going into their senior year of college. Student must also be in good academic standing.    Pursuing a degree in any of the following majors: Management – Operations, Business Administration    Proficient computer skills (Microsoft Office)    Good math and communication skills is preferred    Demonstrated leadership ability.    Energetic & self-motivating    Able to meet deadlines      N   ote:    The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees, and are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel.  Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the employer.     ​#LI-RO1    #ISEVG          Compensation and Benefits:    TTM offers a variety of health and well-being benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, 401K, Flexible Spending Account, Health Savings Account, accident benefits, life insurance, disability benefits, paid vacation & holidays. Benefits are available 1st of the month following date of hire.   Compensation for roles at TTM Technologies varies depending on a wide array of factors including but not limited to the specific office location, role, skill set and level of experience. As required by local law, TTM provides a reasonable range of compensation for roles that may be hired in New York, California and Colorado. For California-based roles, compensation ranges are based upon specific physical locations. jobs.title: Operations Coordinator, Student Care Coordination
jobs.description: Department   College Student Care and Support    About the Department   College Student Care and Support    Job Summary   Reporting to the Associate Director, Student Care Coordination, the Operations Coordinator, Student Care Coordination provides administrative and operational support to the Care and Support Team. The position helps ensure efficient office operations by managing student support processes, shared communications, confidential student records, case assignment workflows, and event and website support. The Operations Coordinator serves as a key administrative partner to the team and helps promote smooth, responsive, and student-centered operations.     Responsibilities     Processes student leave of absence and resumption documentation, including receiving, reviewing, tracking, and routing forms and related materials in accordance with College policies and established procedures.  Conducts outreach to students regarding resumption requirements, offering timely guidance, reminders, and referrals to support a successful return to academic life.  Tracks route and assigns early alert referrals submitted by faculty and other campus partners, ensuring cases are entered, reviewed, and distributed in a timely manner based on office protocols.  Maintains accurate, up-to-date, and confidential student records in Maxient and other applicable systems, including data entry, document management, case notes, and record organization.  Supports office processes with accuracy, discretion, and attention to detail, particularly when handling sensitive student matters, private student information, and time-sensitive documentation.  Manages and respond to shared office email inboxes by monitoring incoming messages, providing accurate and timely information, triaging inquiries, and routing matters to appropriate staff or campus partners.  Communicates professionally and compassionately with students, faculty, staff, and campus partners, serving as a helpful point of contact who represents the office in a responsive and student-centered manner.  Manages the Dean of Students emergency phone process, including coordinating the staff schedule, updating announcements and notifications, and transferring the phone to assigned staff.  Provides general operational support to the Care and Support Team, including scheduling assistance, document preparation, monitoring workflows, maintaining supplies, and supporting day-to-day office operations.  Drafts and produces newsletters and other office communications that share important information, promote resources, highlight upcoming events, and build student awareness of College Care and Support services.  Updates and refreshes website content and online resources so information is current, clear, accessible, and aligned with office services, processes, and deadlines.  Assists with planning events and outreach activities, including coordinating logistics, preparing materials, ordering food and supplies, confirming arrangements, and providing day-of administrative support as needed.  Serves on committees and represent the College Care and Support Team.  Responsible for training office staff on office procedures and compliance protocols. Coordinates special projects. jobs.description: Location:  Woodland Hills, CA (Hybrid)   Company overview  Venbrook Group, LLC is one of the fastest-growing independently owned insurance brokerage, claims, and risk management consulting companies in the United States. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Venbrook operates across multiple U.S. locations through its subsidiaries, including retail brokerage, wholesale brokerage, specialty programs, and claims services. Our culture is approachable, adaptable, and entrepreneurial-spirited, with a commitment to diversity, inclusivity, and respect.   About the role  The Client Executive is accountable for renewing and retaining a designated book of Student Insurance clients. That is the core of the job: leading renewal strategy and carrier negotiations, showing clients what their claims and plan performance mean, and earning the right to keep the business each year. You’ll own the decision-maker relationships at each institution and step in when a claim or service issue needs a more senior hand.   You’ll also own implementation, carrying a sold account from close through to live. The role is based in California because regular travel to client campuses is a significant part of the job. It suits someone with five to seven years of insurance account management experience who is comfortable with data, negotiation, and being the person clients call first.   This role reports to the Senior Vice President, Student Insurance, and works closely with Client Managers, carrier partners, vendors, and Student Insurance leadership.   What you’ll do  Client service and strategy   Own the retention of a designated book of Student Insurance business, and independently market, renew, service, and invoice those accounts.    Own the decision-maker relationships at each institution, typically risk managers, student health center directors, business officers and bursars, athletic directors, and international student services leaders, while the Client Manager handles day-to-day working contacts.    Build strong, trusting client relationships, understanding each client’s needs and responding to all inquiries within 24 business hours.    Lead regular meetings and strategic reviews on plan performance, client concerns, and opportunities to improve service.    Resolve client inquiries and complaints about insurance products, policy changes, benefits, claims, and billing.    Step in on escalated claims and service issues that go beyond what the Client Manager can resolve, and see them through with the client and carrier.    Prepare and present presentations, carrier policies, and reports so clients can review claims data and coverage recommendations.    Own a client service calendar aligned to the academic year, covering enrollment periods, waiver deadlines, and renewal milestones.    Deliver client trainings each year.    Report to the SVP and Student Insurance leadership on account status, financials, servicing, and renewal progress as needed.    Travel approximately 25% of the time to clients across California and at the direction of the SVP.   Renewals, marketing, and analysis   Market, analyze, and negotiate renewals with carriers on behalf of clients to secure competitive premiums and policy terms.    Use actuarial rate setting and claims analysis, including Milliman, to inform renewal strategy and client recommendations.    Prepare renewal contracts, review policies for accuracy, process endorsements and invoices, and set up files.    Explain coverages and policy terms clearly to client stakeholders.    Lead responses to RFPs and public procurement processes, including bid requirements and board approval timelines.    Maintain strong working relationships with national and specialty carrier partners, staying current on products, appetites, and program changes.   Implementation and data   Own new business implementation, internally and externally, carrying each sold account from close to live: kickoff, carrier and vendor setup, enrollment build, and handoff into ongoing service.    Own renewal implementation for existing clients, including plan and rate changes, updated materials, and confirming everything is accurate before the new plan year begins.    Manage enrollment file exchange, including 834 and other formats, and administer SFTP sites and file transfers with carriers and vendors.    Oversee the setup, testing, and accuracy of custom enrollment portals for assigned clients.    Maintain client files and records in Salesforce, AMS360, and other systems, documenting all account activity clearly enough for others to pick up.    Uphold documentation, data-accuracy, and errors-and-omissions (E&O) standards across client records and deliverables.   Compliance and growth   Support compliance across the product portfolio, recognizing that requirements vary by product: ACA-related requirements for student health plans, F-1 and J-1 visa coverage requirements for international student plans, state insurance code and athletic association rules for K-12 and athlete accident plans, and HIPAA across the book.    Find and act on opportunities to grow account revenue by cross-selling other products in the portfolio.    Stay current on student insurance market trends, carrier developments, and legislative and regulatory changes affecting school and student coverage.    Perform additional duties and special projects as assigned. jobs.description: Please note: Due to the regulations regarding working rights, we are only considering applicants enrolled in a Dutch University.    Grow with confidence. Create with impact   At Unilever, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to the  people ,  products, technologies and operations behind some of the world's most recognised consumer brands such as Dove, Vaseline, and Rexona , just to name a few! Working in a global business that reaches  3.4 billion people every day,  you'll help tackle real challenges across technology, innovation, sustainability and beyond - while gaining first-hand insight into how ideas become products at scale. You will gain hands-on experience across different areas of finance, including performance management, financial planning, controlling, business partnering, analytics, and finance transformation.  Depending on the team and business priorities, your responsibilities may include:   Supporting financial planning, forecasting, budgeting and performance management activities across business units and functions.  Analyzing financial, operational and commercial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities and performance drivers.  Assisting in the preparation of reports, dashboards and presentations that support management reviews and business decision-making.  Contributing to projects focused on financial control, cost management, productivity improvement and business performance optimization.  Supporting the development and automation of reporting processes through digital tools, analytics solutions and AI-enabled technologies.  Collaborating with stakeholders across Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, Marketing, Sales, HR and other business functions to support business priorities and strategic initiatives.  Conducting business analyses and research to support investment decisions, process improvements and transformation projects.  Assisting with governance, compliance and risk management activities, where relevant to the business area.    What You'll Learn   During this internship, you will have the opportunity to:   Develop a strong understanding of how finance supports strategic and operational decision-making within a global FMCG business.  Gain exposure to key finance disciplines, including performance management, controlling, forecasting, business partnering and finance transformation.  Strengthen analytical and problem-solving skills through hands-on experience working with financial, operational and commercial data.  Learn how finance collaborates with different business functions to improve performance, manage risk and drive growth.  Build experience with leading digital finance tools, including Excel, Power BI, AI and automation solutions.  Develop stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills by working with cross-functional teams across local, regional and global organizations.  Take ownership of meaningful projects and contribute to real business challenges in a dynamic international environment. jobs.title: Commercial Banking Intern
jobs.description:
Our Commercial Banking Internship is designed to launch your banking career by giving you an immersive, hands-on look at how UMB powers businesses of every size, and you may be considered for the 2028     UMB Banker Development Program.     You’ll step into the world of commercial banking and lending, where we help companies thrive through solutions like treasury management, commercial lending, payments and healthcare financial services.         Markets for UMB's 2028 Banker Development Program will be determined at a later date. However, the Commercial Banking Line of Business has several markets, and candidates willing to relocate to multiple markets are preferred. Markets could include:    Salt Lake City Fresno Albuquerque Fort Worth Denver CO Springs Des Moines Kansas City Lubbock/Midland/Odessa Milwaukee/Madison Minneapolis Oklahoma City Tulsa Phoenix St. Louis Rockford Springfield Wichita    The Commercial Banking Internship will be part of UMB's Summer Internship Program starting on June 2nd, 2027 to August 6th, 2027. jobs.description: Job Description:             Vertex Inc: 2027 Summer MBA / Graduate Internship Program      12-week internship: May 24–August 13  or  June 7–August 27, 2027      Location: Remote within the U.S. or Canada, with one onsite event, Launchpad       Join a Leader in Tax Technology and Global SaaS Innovation      Every company that sells across borders has to calculate, collect, and report indirect tax correctly, in real time, in thousands of jurisdictions. Experience:  3–5+ years of prior experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a technical role such as software engineering, data science, or technical product management preferred.       Strategic Mindset:  Ability to distill complex data into actionable insights and business recommendations.       Communication Skills:  Exceptional ability to build executive-ready presentations and influence decisions through storytelling.       Analytical Rigor:  Strong financial modeling and market analysis skills.       Collaborative Leadership:  Proven ability to navigate cross-functional teams and drive alignment in fast-paced environments. jobs.description: Investing in You, join a 100-year-old, family-owned leader in Ag – and grow with us! During this 12-week program, you'll learn from experienced finance professionals, tackle real-world projects, and develop working knowledge of financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and business decision support within a leading agribusiness organization. You'll have the opportunity to present your internship learnings directly to leadership. This is more than just an internship. It's your chance to make a real impact, build professional knowledge, and sharpen your abilities in a dynamic, results-driven environment. Successful completion of the PLOT program can also earn you a scholarship between $1,000 and $3,000.        Role Overview:       As a Wilbur-Ellis Finance Intern, you'll gain experience in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, reporting, and business performance management. You'll work alongside finance professionals to support projects that help drive informed business decisions and contribute to the financial success of the organization.     Responsibilities may include analyzing financial and operational data, supporting budgeting and forecasting activities, assisting with financial reporting, identifying trends and business insights, developing data visualizations and presentations, conducting research, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to support strategic initiatives and process improvements.     You'll have the opportunity to share your ideas, contribute innovative solutions, and develop an understanding of how finance partners with business leaders to drive growth and operational excellence. At the conclusion of your internship, you'll prepare and present a final PowerPoint presentation highlighting your project work, key learnings, and overall experience.        What You Bring to the Role:       As an intern, we understand you may not already have extensive professional experience. We are seeking a college student pursuing a degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Agricultural Business, or a related field with an interest in finance and business strategy.     Overall, we are looking for someone with strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills; attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy; the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively; proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other analytical tools; intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn; a self-starter who is eager to contribute ideas and collaborate with others; and someone who brings their full self to work each day. We want to help you grow, and we want to learn from you, too.        Examples of What You May Gain:        Exposure to corporate finance, financial planning and analysis, and business decision support within a leading agribusiness organization       Experience supporting budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and business analysis activities       Opportunities to collaborate with finance professionals, business leaders, and cross-functional teams across the organization       Development of analytical, financial modeling, problem-solving, and presentation skills       Hands-on experience interpreting financial data, identifying trends, and providing actionable business insights       Exposure to financial systems, reporting tools, and industry best practices       Mentorship from experienced finance professionals and business leaders       A deeper understanding of how financial performance impacts business strategy, operational decisions, and long-term growth       Real-world experience contributing to projects that support financial excellence, business performance, and organizational success               Compensation and Benefits:        In compliance with all states and cities requiring transparency of pay, the base compensation for this position ranges from $17.00 to $24.00 per hour. jobs.title: Assistant Director of Student Financial Aid Operations
jobs.description: Williams College is pleased to announce an opening for an  Assistant Director of Student Financial Aid Operations  in Student Financial Services. Reporting to the Associate Director of Student Financial Services, this position will be integral in the onboarding of a new ERP system (Workday) while also supporting the first full cycle of the new financial aid software (PowerFAIDS) to support our students.     Undergraduates come to Williams from around the world and a wide variety of backgrounds. About 15% are first-generation college students, 18% are Pell Grant recipients, and 42% are U.S. students of color. Ten percent are international and they represent 96 countries around the world. The college is deeply committed to access and affordability. Williams was the first college in the country to offer All-Grant financial aid awards eliminating the need for students to work or borrow as part of their required financial aid awards. More than 52% of enrolled students receive financial aid and among those students, the net average cost is about $13,000. More than 28% pay nothing at all, and indebtedness rates at graduation from Williams College are among the nation’s lowest.      As the higher education landscape continues to evolve, we seek a strategic partner to help imagine and implement the next generation of Williams’ longstanding commitment to access and affordability. Student Financial Services plans to utilize the strengths, experience, and interests of our new colleague in order to provide the greatest opportunity for professional growth and advance the ambitious goals of the department. Our expectation is that the successful candidate will excel at working in a community that is broadly diverse and is:        Adept at navigating complex federal, state, and institutional financial aid systems    Able to speak with ease to diverse audiences    Comfortable curating and analysing data from various sources    Creative problem solver    Independent thinker who enjoys working with a complex, deadline-driven team that requires flexibility and openness to change    Able to build strong partnerships with key colleagues across campus to ensure the best experience for all students.       Requirements:      A Bachelor’s degree is required.    At least 3 years of experience in financial aid or related secondary or higher education administration is required.     Experience in Workday and/or PowerFAIDS is preferred.    Skilled in Microsoft Excel and other analysis tools    Strong organizational and operational skills, and exceptional oral and written communication skills    Ability to work extended hours during peak periods      This is a full-time, year-round, regular appointment. The pay range for this position is between $62,000-$72,000 commensurate with experience. Application review will begin  December 15, 2026.       A cover letter is  required  in order for your application to be considered.  In your letter, please address how your experience is relevant to the position, how you’ve managed operational aspects of the financial aid process, how you’ve enjoyed populations you’ve worked with professionally, and what draws you to this role.     Hybrid on-site/remote work arrangements may be available up to 2 days per week with approval for employees based in NY, MA, CT, or VT, subject to review and revision as policy evolves. This position requires a minimum 3 days per week of on-campus, in person work, following a fully in-person onboarding period.     Please visit     careers.williams.edu     to apply.     ALL employees must have completed an I-9 BEFORE they can begin work.     Employment at Williams is contingent on the verification of background information submitted by the applicant, including the completion of a criminal record check, and education when applicable. Decisions regarding appointments, promotions, and conditions of employment comply with applicable federal or state law prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, sex, national origin, religion, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, ancestry, or military service.   It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.    Beyond meeting fully its legal obligations for non-discrimination, Williams College is committed to building a diverse and inclusive community where members from all backgrounds can live, learn and thrive. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process please feel free to contact us via phone at (413) 597-2681 or email at  hr@williams.edu .

Role summary:     As a Market Strategy Data Science Intern, you will analyze demographic, competitive and geographic trends that inform real estate and market growth strategies. You will collaborate with cross-functional partners to evaluate site opportunities, identify patterns in large datasets and generate predictive insights for store location planning and portfolio optimization.     About the team:     Walmart Real Estate supports the places and physical assets that enable Walmart to serve customers and communities. Our work spans the full real estate lifecycle and brings together teams across strategy, portfolio and development, design, construction, facilities, fuel and convenience, data, technology, and other supporting functions.     This graduate/MBA internship supports Market Strategy through data science, artificial intelligence, and geospatial analysis. The role will help identify high-priority growth opportunities and strengthen data-informed real estate decisions.     What you'll do:       Analyze demographic, competitive and geographic data to support market prioritization.  Use SQL, machine learning and geospatial methods to identify patterns and generate actionable insights.  Build a market prioritization model in Power BI.  Explore an agentic AI and optimization solution to improve market and site opportunity decisions.  Translate analytical results into recommendations for market strategy and real estate leaders.  Collaborate with data science, real estate, strategy and other cross-functional teams.  Document assumptions, methods and findings and deliver a final presentation.  
  What you'll bring:       Currently pursuing a MBA or graduate degree in data science, analytics, business, economics, computer science, engineering or a related field.  Ability to work with structured data and communicate analytical findings to non-technical partners.  Strong analytical, problem-solving and presentation skills.  Ability to work independently while collaborating in a deadline-driven environment.  Experience with SQL, Power BI, machine learning, geospatial analysis or optimization.  Coursework or project experience involving artificial intelligence, predictive analytics or real estate strategy.  Interest in applying advanced analytics to growth, site selection and portfolio decisions.

jobs.description: Job Title:  Summer 2027 Internship - Phoenix, AZ - Accounting      Location:  CityScape      What you'll do:  Launch your career with Western Alliance Bank in our  Summer Internship Program!  You’ll gain real-life experience and explore what it’s like to work as part of an organization that exemplifies people, performance and possibilities.   As an intern, you’ll work on challenging projects in your specific area of study and receive support from a mentor. Our interns work alongside world-class professionals in a fast-paced, professional setting, giving you an opportunity to make an impact and apply the knowledge and skills you’ve learned through your education.   Western Alliance Bancorporation is one of the country's top-performing banking companies.  Its primary subsidiary, Western Alliance Bank, Member FDIC; offers a full spectrum of commercial banking solutions and consumer products.  All delivered with outstanding service by banking and mortgage experts who put customers first.   In this paid internship, you’ll be empowered to work on challenging and complex issues in a collaborative environment with other talented interns. Over the 10-week program, you’ll participate in business projects, mentoring, leadership development training and team-building activities designed to set you up for professional success. The summer Internship program runs June through August, with flexible dates available, based on school schedules. Interns who perform well and demonstrate a commitment to our values of integrity, creativity, teamwork, passion and excellence may be extended employment opportunities with Western Alliance Bank.  We're looking for individuals who are passionate and entrepreneurial, just like our clients. Specifically, we're looking for top-performers interested in pursuing careers in Commercial Banking.    What you'll need:     Undergraduate students currently enrolled in a related field of study.  GPA of 3.0 or higher.  Strong analytical, conceptual, communication and organizational skills.  Ability to self-motivate and work productively without supervision.  An interest in working in the Commercial Business Banking industry.  To be eligible for this program, you must be authorized to work in the U.S. on a permanent basis. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Western Alliance Bank will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including Optional Practical Training (OPT) or Curricular Practical Training (CPT).          Benefits you’ll love:  We offer all the important things you'd want — like competitive salaries, an ownership stake in the company, medical and dental insurance, time off, a great 401k matching program, tuition assistance program, an employee volunteer program, and a wellness program. In addition, you’ll have the opportunity to bolster your business knowledge, learning the ins and outs of how successful companies operate and manage their finances, giving you invaluable hands-on experience to help grow your career!     About the company:   Western Alliance Bank, Member FDIC, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Western Alliance Bancorporation. Serving clients nationwide, Western Alliance Bank includes six legacy bank brands — Alliance Association Bank, Alliance Bank of Arizona, Bank of Nevada, Bridge Bank, First Independent Bank and Torrey Pines Bank — that remain part of the company’s heritage, as well as AmeriHome Mortgage, a Western Alliance Bank Company. jobs.description: Job Description     Job Description:    The Student Financial Services Counselor plays a critical role in supporting the recruitment, advising, retention, and financial operations of the institution. These contributions are achieved by providing comprehensive financial aid and student accounts service to students and families. Professionals occupying this position are expected to be proficient in the best practices associated with the administration, reporting, and compliance parameters required by state, federal, and institutional financial assistance organizations. Acting as a comprehensive resource to current and prospective graduate, undergraduate, and professional development students, Student Financial Services Counselor act as the primary service provider for all financial aid and student account counseling. The professional scope for this position includes the capacity to provide guidance on aid eligibility, satisfactory academic progress, student lending/repayment options, institutional payment plans, aid related tax exposure, student employment and health insurance compliance.      Key Responsibilities   :     Support the administration, processing, and assessment of multiple financial aid vehicles including federal, state, and institutionally sponsored aid programs for assigned student caseload.    Provide financial assistance and payment counseling to current and prospective students/ families. Address questions regarding all dimensions of aid eligibility, professional judgement parameters, aid renewals, appeals, federal/private loans, external scholarships, student employment and alternative payment options.    Ensure compliance with institutional, federal and state financial aid regulations, including Title IV policies and procedures. Participate in internal and external audit process.    Advise and monitor payment plans, coordinate with students on outstanding balances. Assist in the development, implementation and execution of policies for collections, account holds, and financial appeals. Oversee student billing, tuition payments, refunds, and account reconciliations.    Participate in current and prospective student programing. Represent and promote the full scope of student financial services at virtual and in-person events. Programs include financial wellness days, FAFSA completion events, webinars, advising fairs, and open house experiences.    Assume operational leadership roles over designated projects and functions. These focus areas are determined by the Associate Vice President for Student Financial Services and may include audit prep, compliance, payment plans, collections, third party payments, outside scholarships, state affiliations, federal compliance, veteran benefits, and graduate programs.        Qualifications  :    Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, higher education administration, or a related field (Master’s preferred).    1-3+ years of experience in student accounts, financial aid, or related financial services in higher education.    Strong knowledge of federal and state financial aid regulations, as well as student accounts policies.    Commitment to participate and engage in ongoing professional development including attendance and presentation opportunities available within state, regional and national professional organizations.    Experience with student information systems (e.g., Banner, Flywire, Campus Logic, Slate, Workday) and financial aid/loan portals.    Excellent, detail-oriented communication, problem-solving, and customer service skills.    Ability to work collaboratively across departments and handle sensitive financial matters with discretion. jobs.title: Applied Scientist (Economics) Intern
jobs.description: About the team  The forecasting and business economics group at Zillow shapes planning and drives decision making across Zillow’s businesses. Embedded in the finance organization, our team prioritizes research projects that directly impact the company’s bottom line and growth.   We bring together forecasters, economists, applied scientists, data scientists, and data visualization engineers to build forecasts and craft research that elevates how our businesses operate. We transform our industry-leading data with our expertise in statistics and economics into actionable insights that inform decisions at every level of the company. Our work combines state of the art quantitative methods across forecasting, data science, and causal inference to help answer practical questions for  our business leaders.    About the role    At Zillow, interns do meaningful work that contributes to the business from day one. Our 9 week summer internship program, running June 14th through August 13th, gives students the opportunity to bring their ideas and perspectives to real projects alongside Zillow teams.     Interns build hands-on experience, connect with mentors and leaders, and take part in learning and community experiences with their intern cohort. Our 2027 internships are based in Seattle and follow a hybrid schedule, with interns generally working together in person Tuesday through Thursday.  Eligible interns will receive a stipend to help offset summer housing and relocation costs.      We’re looking for students who are analytical and detail-oriented with the ability to create structure from ambiguity. You have an intense curiosity to learn and can do so in a fast-paced dynamic environment. If you are not afraid of working with large amounts of data, you’ll get the chance to make it all come together into meaningful metrics used to make strategic business decisions.     During your internship, you will have opportunities to:      Partner with your manager and stakeholders to translate open-ended business questions into an analytical approach, with clear deliverables that will directly translate to tangible benefits to revenue.     Explore, clean, and validate housing, economic, business, or financial data; document assumptions and identify data-quality issues.    Build and compare models to support prediction and forecasting.    Transform observational data into causal models using clever identification    Design experiments to improve how we price and operate across our different businesses     Evaluate models using appropriate baselines and time-based validation, and communicate uncertainty, limitations, and trade-offs.    Investigate trends, forecast errors, and drivers of business performance to develop actionable insights.    Create reproducible analyses, visualizations, or reporting workflows that help partners understand and use your findings.    Share your approach, results, and recommendations with technical and nontechnical audiences, and document your work for a clear handoff.       This role has been categorized as an Office position. “Office” employees regularly work at an existing ZG corporate office for approximately 80 to 100 percent of their time each month. Employees must live within reasonable commuting distance of their designated ZG office. ZG has not defined a reasonable distance, and expects employees will use judgment in determining this for themselves and understand the implications re: time commitment and cost of daily commute.    In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $104,000.00 - $166,000.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.    Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location.    Who you are     Currently pursuing a Masters or PhD in statistics, economics, data science, applied mathematics, quantitative finance, or a related quantitative field, with an expected graduation between December 2027 and Summer 2028.     Strong foundation in probability, statistics, and regression analysis, with exposure to econometrics. Specifically time-series and causal analysis through coursework and research experience.    Use AI tools to accelerate and expand their work without outsourcing their own thinking to it.    Can use Python or similar to prepare data, conduct analysis, and build models. Even if you’re not writing code anymore, we expect an ability to express statistical concepts clearly through pseudocode and think through edgecases when designing systems.     Can explain analytical findings clearly and collaborate with people who bring different perspectives and expertise including non technical stakeholders.    Move quickly and ambitiously without sacrificing attention to detail; enjoy zooming in and out based on context.     Approach problems thoughtfully: you check your assumptions, validate results, and distinguish what the data supports from what remains uncertain.    Are interested in applying quantitative methods to housing markets, business forecasting, and financial decision-making. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.       How we work is a key part of that transformation.
